# Critical review - solmq-conn-util

Date: 2026-10-06
Commit: ec00d28 on main, working tree dirty
Previous report: none
Scope: all areas
Stacks: Go (go.md), bash (bash.md), GitHub Actions (github-actions.md), containers (containers.md, applied to the rendered compose/quadlet/Kubernetes artifacts); PowerShell (scripts/dev.ps1) and the HTML/JavaScript spec generator on the core checklist only
Graph: reused, stale by 2 commits (built from 94e73e13, HEAD ec00d28); 2179 nodes, 8150 links, 133 communities
Dynamic checks: user-run: dev.sh vet, go test -race, go mod tidy -diff, bash -n (all clean); docker compose config run without a file; see Dynamic checks

## Summary

| Severity | New | Still open | Fixed since last | Total open |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Blocker | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| Major | 27 | 0 | 0 | 27 |
| Minor | 219 | 0 | 0 | 219 |
| Nit | 96 | 0 | 0 | 96 |
| Suspected (uncounted) | 36 | 0 | 0 | 36 |

solmq-conn-util is a well-structured Go CLI: one command model drives usage, docs and four completion scripts, every external call goes through an argv-only runner, and the test suite is large and mostly behavioural. The review still found one blocker and 27 majors, almost all in the seams the design document declares safe: kubernetes fields with no validator (resources, PVC storage, the download image) are written raw into the manifest, so a newline in env.yaml injects sibling keys; the generated Kubernetes, compose and quadlet artifacts emit no security posture at all; the status account password is redrawn on every render; and podman's `unless-stopped` default is written into a systemd unit that does not understand it. The three platforms diverge in how credentials, stores, health checks and the systemctl identity are handled, and the status/logs/cli verbs probe for write permission they never need. Test gaps cluster where the code talks to real engines (podman deploy, libs download, the status script), and the docs lag the code in a few dozen places, mostly the user guide and the generator page. This is the first run, so there is no trend; 36 findings stay suspected because they depend on runtime behaviour of systemd, kubectl, busybox or a browser that this read-only review could not exercise.

## Top risks

1. CR-0001 [blocker] resources, pvc storage and download.image reach the manifest with no charset gate in checkKube/checkLibs - internal/yamlwriter/yamlwriter.go:18-22 - The project knows the rule (validate.go:829-830 applies it to nfs.path) but four kubernetes-only values skip it. env.yaml `memory: "1Gi\n securityContext:\n privileged: true"` is a legal YAML double-quoted scalar; yaml.v3 decodes the \n; validate.Run reports nothing; quoteRes returns the value unchanged because it is not ^[0-9]+$; line 520 writes `memory: 1Gi` followed by the injected lines at the container-field indentation; `deploy --platform kubernetes` pipes that document to `kubectl apply -f -` (main.go:537-547).
2. CR-0002 [major] CI never gates code changes: no push/PR trigger for Go sources and no schedule for the scanner - .github/workflows/ci.yml:12-24 - This is documented and deliberate, so judge it by impact.
3. CR-0003 [major] actDocker writes its scratch compose file as <envDir>/docker-compose.yml, mode 0644, and keeps it after a failed run - cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:583-586 - GenerateDocker inlines the rendered application.yml under compose `configs: ... content: |` (dockergen.go renderContentConfig), and consolidate renders the solmq-status password into that document as a literal. 2. actDocker writes this document to <envDir>/docker-compose.yml with mode 0644 -- world-readable on a shared host -- for the duration of `docker compose up/down`, and deliberately leaves it on disk whenever the child fails (line 591-592), typically in a directory kept under version control beside env.yaml. 3.
4. CR-0004 [major] pm case in TestPlatformAliasesResolveToCanonical writes a real unit into the developer's ~/.config - cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:2892-2913 - The pm iteration runs the full deploy path through dispatch: actPodman -> ResolveQuadletScope -> podmanDeploy.
5. CR-0005 [major] Namespace occupancy probe cannot see RBAC, policy, ingress or custom resources, so an occupied namespace is reported empty and offered for cascading deletion - cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go:32-37 - kubectl's `all` category is only pods, services, replicationcontrollers, daemonsets, deployments, replicasets, statefulsets, jobs, cronjobs and horizontalpodautoscalers.
6. CR-0006 [major] Write probe `can-i create deployment` in preflight for status/logs/cli refuses view-only RBAC operators - cmd/solmq-conn-util/shell.go:182-187 - An operator holding a view-style ClusterRole plus pods/log and pods/exec (the permissions status, logs and cli actually use) runs `status`, `logs` or `cli` on kubernetes. 2. actStatus/actLogs/actShell call preflight with runner.ActionDeploy, so runner.Preflight builds `kubectl auth can-i create deployment [--namespace ns]`. 3. kubectl answers `no` and exits 1 (can-i encodes the answer in its status), so OS.Run returns an error. 4.
7. CR-0007 [major] collectApplication drops --user/--management-port whenever a status script is already present - cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:753-817 - The port and account an operator passes are baked into the script text (statusscript.Render) and only reach the container through InstallScript. 2.
8. CR-0008 [major] Generator page's JavaScript port runs under no automated gate; TestGeneratorPageGoldenInSync proves only that the embedded copy equals the Go golden - docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:140-142 - The thing that can drift is the JS port of validate/consolidate/render/tls/uuid; the Go test keeps its oracle (the embedded golden) fresh but never executes the port against it, so the comparison at html:3133 happens only when a human clicks Self-test.
9. CR-0009 [major] emitBindingOptions passes consumer/producer keys that duplicate destination-type and durable-subscription-name - internal/consolidate/consolidate.go:296-300 - Three merge points write operator-supplied mapping keys into a mapping the tool also writes fixed keys into, with no collision check: (a) a JMS/Solace binding's consumer:/producer: block next to destination-type and durable-subscription-name; (b) solace-defaults next to host, msg-vpn, client-username, client-password and api-properties under solace.java; (c) the same solace-defaults under the leader-election session. validate has no check on passthrough keys at all (grep for passthrough, Consumer, Producer, SolaceDefaults in internal/validate/validate.go finds only the leader-session binding-fields check at 493-498).
10. CR-0010 [major] Teardown manifest still carries resolved credential values and requires every secret, the registry password and the .jks files just to delete - internal/deploy/deploy.go:169-182 - `kubectl delete -f -` needs only apiVersion/kind/metadata of each document, yet the teardown path renders the full Secret bodies: Render has no Teardown branch around stringData/data, and gen resolves every credential, re-reads the store files and builds the dockerconfigjson before it.

## Findings by area

### design

#### CR-0039 [minor] [new] cliFlag.AppliesTo duplicates cliVerb.Flags membership by hand and nothing gates the two

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands.go:259-293, cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands.go:296-476, cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands_doc_test.go:117-204, cmd/solmq-conn-util/abbreviation.go:129
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    commands.go:265  {Short: allowCommandFlagName, ..., AppliesTo: bt + "deploy" + bt + "/" + bt + "remove" + bt + "/" + bt + "status" + bt + "/" + bt + "logs" + bt + "/" + bt + "cli" + bt, ...}
    commands.go:313  Flags: []string{platformFlagName, "-e", allowCommandFlagName}, (deploy) ... 323 (remove) ... 338 (status) ... 374 (logs) ... 393 (cli) each list allowCommandFlagName
    commands.go:259  AppliesTo: "all except " + bt + "examples" + bt + "/" + bt + "version" + bt + "/" + bt + "auto-complete" + bt + "/" + bt + "help" + bt
    commands.go:644  add("| " + flagSpan(f) + " | " + f.AppliesTo + " | " + f.Meaning + " |")
    abbreviation.go:129  add(f.AppliesTo + ".")   -- the --platform AppliesTo is also the "Platform abbreviations" verb list
    commands_doc_test.go:184-194  checks only that every flag is listed by at least one verb; no test reads AppliesTo

Why it matters: The flag table in commands.md, the --platform sentence in both generated docs and the abbreviation page's "Accepted ... by:" list all come from AppliesTo, a free-text field maintained separately from the Flags lists that drive the help pages and the completion scripts. Today the 29 entries agree (checked one by one), but adding a flag to a verb's Flags, or a verb to a flag, leaves AppliesTo stale with no test failing -- the byte gates would simply pin the stale table once regenerated. The pattern is the same "two tables for one fact" the file's own header warns about. A test that derives each flag's verb set from cliVerbs and compares it with AppliesTo (inverting the sense for the one "all except" spelling) closes it; deriving AppliesTo in the renderer would remove the duplication entirely.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands_doc_test.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands_doc_test.go
@@ -204,0 +205,27 @@
+
+// TestFlagAppliesToMatchesVerbFlags gates the hand-written AppliesTo prose
+// against the verbs whose Flags actually carry the flag: a flag added to a
+// verb without updating its AppliesTo (or the reverse) fails here instead of
+// shipping a flag table that disagrees with the help pages and completion.
+// -e is spelled as an exclusion list, so its sense is inverted.
+func TestFlagAppliesToMatchesVerbFlags(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, f := range cliFlags {
+		except := strings.HasPrefix(f.AppliesTo, "all except ")
+		for _, v := range cliVerbs {
+			uses := false
+			for _, sh := range v.Flags {
+				if sh == f.Short {
+					uses = true
+				}
+			}
+			listed := strings.Contains(f.AppliesTo, bt+v.Name+bt)
+			if except {
+				uses = !uses
+			}
+			if listed != uses {
+				t.Errorf("flag %s: AppliesTo %q disagrees with the Flags of verb %q", f.Long, f.AppliesTo, v.Name)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}
```


#### CR-0050 [minor] [new] abbreviation.go documents set aliases as accepted while runDownload and the completion renderers match set words by canonical name only, and no test guards the gap

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion_test.go:493-498, cmd/solmq-conn-util/abbreviation.go:112-119, cmd/solmq-conn-util/abbreviation_doc_test.go:108-115, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:1036-1041, cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands.go:861-878, cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:302, cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:754, cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:783
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    abbreviation.go:112-118
     112  // Sets are the third command level (download jar mq|syslog). None of
     113  // them carries an alias today; walking them anyway means one that is
     114  // added later lands on this page without a second edit here.
     115  for _, s := range tg.Sets {
     116      for _, a := range s.Aliases {
    abbreviation.go:154-156 (page text): "An abbreviation is accepted wherever its canonical word is ..."
    main.go:1036-1038
    1036  setArg := pos[1]
    1037  set, ok := downloadSets[setArg]
    1038  if !ok {
    commands.go:866-875 (resolveTarget): loops v.Targets and tg.Aliases only; never tg.Sets.
    completion.go:302  add("        " + aliasPattern(tg) + ") printf " + bashQuote(itemNames(tg.Sets)) + " ;;")
    completion.go:754  "; and not __fish_seen_subcommand_from " + itemNames(tg.Sets)
    completion_test.go:493-498: sets get plainText(s.Summary) and assertShellSafeName(t, "set", s.Name) only; s.Aliases is never read.

Why it matters: cliTarget.Sets is a []cliTarget (commands.go:222), so a set can carry Aliases. The abbreviation renderer walks them (abbreviation.go:115-119) and TestAbbreviationDocCoversModel demands a row for each (abbreviation_doc_test.go:108-115), and the page text promises every listed abbreviation is accepted wherever its canonical word is. But runDownload resolves the set word with a direct lookup in downloadSets (main.go:1037) and resolveTarget never descends into Sets (commands.go:866-875), so a set alias would exit 2 as an unknown set; the completion renderers offer and recognise sets through itemNames only (completion.go:302, 754, 783), never itemSeenNames or aliasPattern, so fish would keep offering sets after the alias was typed; and TestCompletionModelMetadataComplete charset-checks set names but not set aliases, although every other alias kind is gated there. No set has an alias today, so nothing is broken yet; the first one added would be documented-but-rejected with every gate green -- the exact defect TestGenerateConfigTargetAliasResolves (test.md:1092) exists to prevent for target aliases. The cheapest guard is a tripwire in the metadata test until the dispatch and renderers resolve set aliases; the patch adds it.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion_test.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion_test.go
@@ -493,6 +493,13 @@ func TestCompletionModelMetadataComplete(t *testing.T) {
 			for _, s := range tg.Sets {
 				if plainText(s.Summary) == "" {
 					t.Errorf("set %q under %q %q has an empty Summary", s.Name, v.Name, tg.Name)
 				}
 				assertShellSafeName(t, "set", s.Name)
+				// abbreviation.go renders a set alias as accepted, but runDownload
+				// (downloadSets) and the completion renderers match set words by
+				// canonical name only; until they resolve aliases, one would be
+				// documented and rejected.
+				if len(s.Aliases) != 0 {
+					t.Errorf("set %q under %q %q declares aliases %v, which runDownload and the completion renderers do not resolve", s.Name, v.Name, tg.Name, s.Aliases)
+				}
 			}
```

#### CR-0055 [minor] [new] Dead name-first sortInstances/sortRefs order overridden by namespace-first statusreport.SortInstances

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/instances.go:320-345, internal/statusreport/statusreport.go:569-579, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:421-421, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:455-459, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:572-572, docs/userguide.md:2897-2898, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:421, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:455-458, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:572, cmd/solmq-conn-util/instances.go:327-345, internal/statusreport/statusreport.go:572-579
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    status.go:455-458: "Alphabetical, so the row an operator counts to is the one --pod <index> selects. kubectl usually returns this order already; docker and podman do not, and the two verbs have to agree." / `sortInstances(insts)`; status.go:572 `sortInstances(insts)` again; then status.go:421, after both collectors return: `statusreport.SortInstances(rep.Instances)`. instances.go:327-334 sortRefs: name first, then namespace; instances.go:338-345 sortInstances: Name then Namespace, "so an index and the table it indexes into cannot drift apart". statusreport.go:569-579 SortInstances: "orders instances by namespace then name" -- `if in[i].Namespace != in[j].Namespace { return in[i].Namespace < in[j].Namespace }`. main_test.go:5693 TestSortIsByNameThenNamespace pins the first order; nothing pins that the two agree.

Why it matters: collect() re-sorts the list the collectors already sorted, with a different key, so the sortInstances calls in status.go are dead work and the comment above them describes an order the final table does not necessarily have. Today no run can observe the disagreement: indexes are refused under --all (the only cross-namespace case), and a single namespace makes the two keys collapse to name order. The docs' promise ("the same order status prints", commands.go logs/cli Detail) therefore rests on a coincidence rather than on one comparator, and the next change that lets an index address a cross-namespace list (or a docker list with per-project grouping) breaks it silently. One comparator, used by both sides, is the fix; the diff below makes instances.go delegate to the report's order so the index side provably matches the table (TestSortIsByNameThenNamespace would need its expectation flipped).

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/instances.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/instances.go
@@ -327,19 +327,15 @@
 func sortRefs(refs []instanceRef) {
 	sort.Slice(refs, func(i, j int) bool {
-		if refs[i].name != refs[j].name {
-			return refs[i].name < refs[j].name
+		if refs[i].namespace != refs[j].namespace {
+			return refs[i].namespace < refs[j].namespace
 		}
-		return refs[i].namespace < refs[j].namespace
+		return refs[i].name < refs[j].name
 	})
 }
 
-// sortInstances puts a report's instances in the same order sortRefs produces,
-// so an index and the table it indexes into cannot drift apart.
+// sortInstances is the report's own order (statusreport.SortInstances), spelled
+// here so the index side and the table side provably share one comparator.
 func sortInstances(insts []statusreport.Instance) {
-	sort.Slice(insts, func(i, j int) bool {
-		if insts[i].Name != insts[j].Name {
-			return insts[i].Name < insts[j].Name
-		}
-		return insts[i].Namespace < insts[j].Namespace
-	})
+	statusreport.SortInstances(insts)
 }
```

Why it matters: The question 'is this instance statically active?' is a property of the leader-election mode, not of a platform, yet each renderer answers it with its own copy of the same two-term comparison (deploy.go:342, dockergen.go:124, podmangen.go:116), each with its own paragraph explaining active_standby. A fourth mode, or a decision that active_active members should not be labelled active, is a three-file change where a miss leaves one platform's `solace-connector/role` label disagreeing with the others -- exactly the cross-platform drift the shared spec.Label* constants were introduced to prevent. The same pattern repeats at smaller scale: `seconds` is defined twice (dockergen.go:226, podmangen.go:104) to spell statusscript's shared cadence constants, and gen.go keeps a private mount type plus four converters (600-628) only because dockergen.Mount and podmangen.Mount are structurally identical types declared twice. The env-quoting trio the lead names (envValueQuote, composeQuote/composeEscape, systemdEnv) is not duplication: each targets a different sink grammar. The diff moves the role rule into spec next to EffectiveMode so the three renderers share one predicate; it needs a table test in internal/spec/defaults_test.go for the four mode values (S5) and a docs/test.md row. The seconds/Mount pair can follow the same route (a statusscript.Seconds helper and one spec.Mount type) in a separate change.

#### CR-0005 [major] [new] Namespace occupancy probe cannot see RBAC, policy, ingress or custom resources, so an occupied namespace is reported empty and offered for cascading deletion

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go:32-37, cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go:157-203, cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go:51-56, cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands.go:330-334, docs/userguide.md:1111-1113, cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go:172-190, cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go:142-148, cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands.go:332-334, cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go:214, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:1505-1519
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    namespace.go:32-37: "`all` covers the workload and service kinds; the three after it do not appear under `all` and are exactly the ones whose loss would hurt most." / `const namespaceProbeTypes = "all,persistentvolumeclaims,secrets,configmaps"`. namespace.go:53-56: `clusterDefaultOccupants = map[string]string{"ConfigMap": "kube-root-ca.crt", "ServiceAccount": "default"}` (ServiceAccounts are not in `all`, so this entry can never match the probe's output; main_test.go:1298 feeds one in by hand). namespace.go:183-203: zero occupants -> prompt "namespace %s holds nothing else -- remove the namespace too?" (or no prompt under --no-prompt) -> `runner.Kubernetes(r, command, runner.ActionRemove, deploy.NamespaceManifest(ns), o.allow)`. commands.go remove Detail: "That is an invariant rather than a default: no flag removes a namespace that still holds someone else's work." docs/userguide.md:1111-1113: "a namespace holding anything this release does not own is never removed -- not interactively, not under --no-prompt, not on any path."

Why it matters: kubectl's `all` category is only pods, services, replicationcontrollers, daemonsets, deployments, replicasets, statefulsets, jobs, cronjobs and horizontalpodautoscalers. The constant adds pvc, secrets and configmaps. Everything else a namespace commonly holds is invisible to the probe: ServiceAccounts, Roles, RoleBindings, Ingresses, NetworkPolicies, ResourceQuotas, LimitRanges, PodDisruptionBudgets, Leases, and every CRD-backed object (cert-manager Certificates, ServiceMonitors, ExternalSecrets, Argo/Flux objects). A namespace pre-provisioned by a platform team -- RoleBindings granting the team access, a ResourceQuota, a LimitRange, a NetworkPolicy -- contains none of the probed kinds once the connector is torn down, so namespaceOccupants returns nothing, the operator is told the namespace "holds nothing else" (false), and under --no-prompt the Namespace is deleted outright; the cascade then destroys the platform team's objects. The code's own exclusion for ServiceAccount:default shows the author expected ServiceAccounts in the result, which they are not. Severity is major because the default path still asks a question (with a false premise); a team running `remove --no-prompt` in CI would experience it as a blocker (data loss). Fix: widen the probe to the built-in kinds that can live in a namespace, and soften the documented invariant to say custom resources are not checked (or additionally probe `kubectl api-resources --namespaced -o name` and query every kind).

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go
@@ -31,10 +31,16 @@
-// namespaceProbeTypes is what the occupancy check asks kubectl for. `all` covers
-// the workload and service kinds; the three after it do not appear under `all`
-// and are exactly the ones whose loss would hurt most.
+// namespaceProbeTypes is what the occupancy check asks kubectl for. `all` is
+// only the workload and service kinds (pods, deployments, replicasets,
+// statefulsets, daemonsets, jobs, cronjobs, hpas, services); every kind after it
+// lives outside `all` and would otherwise go unseen into the cascade: storage
+// and config, the namespace's RBAC and policy objects, and ingress. Custom
+// resources are still not covered, and the docs must say so.
 //
 // A tool-authored constant, never operator input.
-const namespaceProbeTypes = "all,persistentvolumeclaims,secrets,configmaps"
+const namespaceProbeTypes = "all,persistentvolumeclaims,secrets,configmaps," +
+	"serviceaccounts,roles,rolebindings,ingresses,networkpolicies," +
+	"resourcequotas,limitranges,poddisruptionbudgets"
```

Why it matters: 1. An operator holding a view-style ClusterRole plus pods/log and pods/exec (the permissions status, logs and cli actually use) runs `status`, `logs` or `cli` on kubernetes. 2. actStatus/actLogs/actShell call preflight with runner.ActionDeploy, so runner.Preflight builds `kubectl auth can-i create deployment [--namespace ns]`. 3. kubectl answers `no` and exits 1 (can-i encodes the answer in its status), so OS.Run returns an error. 4. Preflight wraps it with preflightHints[kubernetes] = 'log in or select a context first ...' and report() prints 'error: deploy kubernetes failed: preflight failed for kubernetes: exit status 1' with that hint, exit 1 -- before any `get pods`, `logs` or `exec` runs. 5. The verbs that need only read permissions are unusable for exactly the least-privileged users they are meant for, the message blames login, and even the error prefix says 'deploy'. The docs call this probe 'read-only' (userguide 2706) but it tests a write permission that the probe's own comment admits status never needs. The runner has no read action to ask for, which is the fix below (tests pinning `can-i create` for status, e.g. main_test.go:3374, need the new argv).

Why it matters: `kubectl delete -f -` needs only apiVersion/kind/metadata of each document, yet the teardown path renders the full Secret bodies: Render has no Teardown branch around stringData/data, and gen resolves every credential, re-reads the store files and builds the dockerconfigjson before it. Consequences: (1) `remove` fails -- with a message telling the operator to "export it before deploying" -- when a rotated or retired credential variable is no longer in the environment, when image.pass-env is unset, or when a truststore file has moved, although none of them is needed to delete; (2) plaintext credentials are piped into a kubectl process whose only job is deletion, widening where the values travel for no benefit. Fix: in Render, when in.Teardown, emit the Secret documents with metadata only (same names, same order), and in GenerateKubernetes skip ResolveCredentials/resolveStores/resolvePullSecret when opts.Teardown. Why it matters: Unless SECURITY_USER_SOLMQ_STATUS_PASSWORD is exported, every generate/deploy/remove renders a new 32-hex password into application.yml (gen.go:499-503, consolidate.go:479). On podman, a second `deploy` with an unchanged spec (the idempotent re-run an operator reaches for) rewrites <base-dir>/<name>-application.yml in place (main.go:660; os.WriteFile truncates the same inode, so the running container's bind mount shows the new bytes) and then runs only daemon-reload + start (runner.go:596-602): systemd does nothing for an already-active unit, so the JVM keeps the password it loaded at startup. `status application` then execs the script, which reads the NEW password from the mounted file (statusscript.go:200), gets 401 from the actuator, and reports "no answer from .../leaderelection -- check the connector is up ... and that the solmq-status account ... is valid" (statusscript.go:329) for a perfectly healthy instance, until someone restarts the unit. On docker the inlined configs content changes on every re-deploy, so compose recreates the container for a no-op deploy; on Kubernetes the ConfigMap changes on every deploy for no reason (subPath pods keep the old file, so status stays consistent there, as docs/userguide.md:1283-1291 notes). The determinism claims in DEVELOPMENT.md:192-194 and userguide.md:3064-3066 are false for every artifact that embeds application.yml. What would confirm: `deploy --platform podman` twice with no spec change, then `status application`. Fixes, in order of preference: (a) make the generated value stable per instance (e.g. derive it with HMAC-SHA256 from a per-spec secret the operator exports once, or persist the generated value beside the spec with 0600), so re-renders are byte-identical and the docs become true again; or (b) at minimum make runner.PodmanDeploy `restart` an already-active unit (or `systemctl try-restart`) so the file and the process never disagree, and document that docker recreates the container on every deploy. The env override is documented (userguide.md:1003-1006) but the failure mode on podman is not.

Why it matters: Kubernetes: the pod template is a pure function of names and labels, so a ConfigMap or Secret change leaves it byte-identical; apply updates the objects, the subPath mounts never refresh, and the JVM only reads configtree/application.yml at start -- `deploy` reports ok with pods on the previous workflow set, password or status script. This is documented with a manual follow-up, but the tool still presents the deploy as complete. Podman: the same deploy rewrites application.yml in place, replaces each secret object, reloads the generator and calls `systemctl start`; start does nothing on an already-active unit, so the running container keeps the secret files it was created with and the JVM keeps its parsed config -- not documented anywhere (userguide.md:1563-1566 describes the sequence as if start applied it). @@ -599,10 +599,13 @@ func PodmanDeploy(r Runner, sc QuadletScope, services []string) (string, error)

```diff
 	}

-		o, err = r.Run(Cmd{Argv: sc.systemctlArgs("start", s)})
+		// restart, not start: start is a no-op on a unit that is already active,
+		// so a redeploy would leave the running container on the files and
+		// secrets it was created with. restart starts a stopped unit as well.
+		o, err = r.Run(Cmd{Argv: sc.systemctlArgs("restart", s)})
 		out.WriteString(o)
 		if err != nil {
-			return out.String(), fmt.Errorf("systemctl start %s: %w", s, err)
+			return out.String(), fmt.Errorf("systemctl restart %s: %w", s, err)
 		}
```

#### CR-0026 [major] [new] uptime truncation reads Jackson's scientific notation as a one-digit integer after ~116 days

Location: internal/statusreport/parse.go:778, internal/statusreport/statusreport.go:216, internal/statusreport/render.go:280, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:371-378, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:367-369, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:424-428
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    statusscript.go
    368   (metric: sed captures the first "value": number, charset [0-9.eE+-] -- an exponent form is accepted)
    371 UPTIME=$(metric process.uptime)
    372 UPTIME=${UPTIME%%.*}
    373 case "${UPTIME:-x}" in
    374   *[!0-9]*) UPTIME="" ;;
    375 esac
    376 if [ -n "$UPTIME" ]; then
    377   echo "uptime: $((UPTIME / 86400))d $((UPTIME % 86400 / 3600))h $((UPTIME % 3600 / 60))m"
    424 # Heap use, in raw bytes exactly as Micrometer reported them -- the CLI renders
    425 # them as Mi/Gi. Deliberately not converted here: Jackson may serialise a large
    426 # double in scientific notation (4.32013312E8), which busybox integer
    427 # arithmetic would silently read as 4

Why it matters: Micrometer's process.uptime is a double in seconds, and Jackson writes doubles with Java's Double.toString, which switches to scientific notation at or above 1e7 -- 1e7 s is 115.7 days, a routine uptime for a connector. The metric regex captures e.g. 1.0012345E7; line 372 strips everything from the first dot, leaving 1; the digits-only guard at 373-375 passes it; line 377 prints 'uptime: 0d 0h 0m'. An operator reading 0 minutes on a long-running instance will conclude it just restarted, the opposite of the truth, and ParseApplication stores the string verbatim so the JSON carries the same wrong value. The author identified exactly this hazard for heap (424-428) and routed heap bytes raw to the CLI; uptime did not get the same treatment. Minimal fix (patch): refuse to compute from a value carrying an exponent and drop the line truthfully. Better fix: emit the raw seconds like heap and format d/h/m in Go, where ParseQuantity already reads the exponent. TestRenderReportsHealthUptimeAndVersion / TestRenderHeaderNamesEveryReportedFact may pin the current lines and need the same edit.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/statusscript/statusscript.go
+++ b/internal/statusscript/statusscript.go
@@ -369,7 +369,13 @@
 }
 
-UPTIME=$(metric process.uptime)
-UPTIME=${UPTIME%%.*}
+# Jackson writes a double >= 1e7 (about 116 days of uptime) in scientific
+# notation; truncating that at the dot would read 1.0012345E7 as 1, so an
+# exponent drops the line rather than printing a restart that never happened.
+UPTIME=$(metric process.uptime)
+case "$UPTIME" in
+  *[eE]*) UPTIME="" ;;
+  *) UPTIME=${UPTIME%%.*} ;;
+esac
 case "${UPTIME:-x}" in
   *[!0-9]*) UPTIME="" ;;
 esac
```

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/instances.go:92-105, cmd/solmq-conn-util/instances.go:244-251, internal/validate/validate.go:1440-1454, internal/runner/runner.go:665-668, internal/runner/runner.go:921-929, internal/runner/runner.go:974-992
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    validate.go:1446 const shellMeta = ";|&<>()*?[]{}~#!"
    validate.go:1452-1454 func SafeToken(s string) bool { return safeShellChars(s) && !strings.ContainsAny(s, shellMeta) }
    instances.go:96-99 for _, p := range t.pods { if !validate.SafeToken(p) { return s, fmt.Errorf("--pod %q contains an unsafe character ...
    runner.go:923 argv = append(argv, target)            (kubernetes exec: pod positional before -n/-c/--)
    runner.go:929 argv = append(argv, target)            (docker/podman exec: name positional)
    runner.go:975 argv = append(argv, target)            (kubernetes logs)
    runner.go:667 argv = append(argv, names...)          (get pods <names>)

Why it matters: 1. The only check on --pod/--container/--namespace is SafeToken, whose charset is about shells; '-' and '=' are allowed anywhere, so `--pod --kubeconfig=/tmp/x`, `--pod -h` or `--container --privileged` pass the gate. 2. Every sink appends the value as a positional (exec, logs, get pods, inspect, stats), so kubectl/docker parse it as one of their own flags: `kubectl exec -i -t --kubeconfig=/tmp/x -n ns -c connector -- sh` runs against another cluster's config, `-h` prints help with exit 0 and the picker-free path treats it as success. 3. Only the operator's own flags can carry such a value (API-server pod names, engine container names and image refs cannot start with '-'), so this is not a privilege boundary, but it is a wrong result produced silently from a typo, and the fix is one predicate: a name that reaches a positional slot must not start with '-' (or the kubernetes sinks could place the pod after a literal `--` where kubectl allows it). Worth a shared helper beside SafeToken rather than per-call checks.

Why it matters: podman.base-dir is by definition a path on the Linux podman host (the examples use /opt/solmq-connector). On Windows, filepath.IsAbs("/opt/solmq-connector") is false because the path has no volume name, so line 1383 joins it under envDir and gen.go:418 records plan.BaseDir as C:\specs\opt\solmq-connector; pathIn (664) then appends "/connector-application.yml", and podmangen.go:169 emits Volume=C:\specs\opt\solmq-connector/connector-application.yml:/app/external/...:ro -- a mixed-separator Windows path in a systemd unit. This is only reachable from `generate --platform podman` on a Windows workstation (deploy there already fails per the PARB-01 finding), and the user guide calls that output a preview, so the impact is a misleading preview rather than a broken deploy. The compose side is not affected: tls.*.file and libs.dir written as Windows paths render as Windows bind-mount sources, which Docker Desktop's compose accepts. The lead's mode half (0600/0644) is an OS limitation: Go applies only the read-only bit on Windows, which the tests already acknowledge (runner_test.go:621-622, main_test.go:2595-2596) and which is moot while podman deploy cannot run there. #### CR-0075 [minor] [new] isOurs misses the release's own pods: their owner is the ReplicaSet <name>-<hash>, not the Deployment

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go:98-121, cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go:125-138, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:1288-1292, internal/spec/kubernetes.go:325-341, cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go:99-103
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    namespace.go:100-103 // - our own objects, and anything owned by one of them (the ReplicaSets and
     //   Pods behind the Deployment name their owner, so one rule covers them);
    namespace.go:129-136
    129 if owned[it.Metadata.Name] {
    130     return true
    131 }
    132 for _, ref := range it.Metadata.OwnerReferences {
    133     if owned[ref.Name] {
    134         return true
    135     }
    136 }
    main_test.go:1289-1291 name: "a pod we own via ownerReferences", item: `{"kind":"Pod","metadata":{"name":"solmq-connector-7d4-abc","ownerReferences":[{"kind":"ReplicaSet","name":"solmq-connector"}]}}`

Why it matters: 1. owned = CreatedNames() = the deployment name and its derived objects. 2. A Deployment-managed ReplicaSet is named <deployment>-<pod-template-hash>, so a Pod's ownerReference is that hashed name, never the deployment name; the test fixture encodes a ReplicaSet named exactly 'solmq-connector', which the controller never produces. 3. `kubectl delete -f -` uses background cascading by default: the Deployment object is gone when kubectl returns, while the garbage collector deletes the ReplicaSet and pods afterwards, so at probe time the pods typically still exist with no deletionTimestamp. 4. isOurs therefore returns false for them, removeNamespace prints 'namespace X still holds N resource(s) this release does not own: pod/<our pod>' and keeps the namespace -- the safe direction, but the feature misfires on the common case and the message blames a foreign owner for the tool's own pods. Closing ownership over the ReplicaSets present in the same listing fixes both without widening what counts as ours.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/namespace.go
@@ -109,9 +109,21 @@ func namespaceOccupants(doc string, owned map[string]bool) ([]string, error) {
 	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(strings.TrimSpace(doc)), &list); err != nil {
 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading the namespace contents: %w", err)
 	}
+	// A Deployment's pods are owned by its ReplicaSet (<deployment>-<hash>),
+	// not by the Deployment, so ownership is closed over one level: every
+	// ReplicaSet one of our names owns is ours, and so is whatever it owns.
+	ours := make(map[string]bool, len(owned))
+	for k := range owned {
+		ours[k] = true
+	}
+	for _, it := range list.Items {
+		if it.Kind == "ReplicaSet" && isOurs(it, owned) {
+			ours[it.Metadata.Name] = true
+		}
+	}
 	var out []string
 	for _, it := range list.Items {
-		if isOurs(it, owned) || isClusterDefault(it) {
+		if isOurs(it, ours) || isClusterDefault(it) {
 			continue
 		}
 		out = append(out, strings.ToLower(it.Kind)+"/"+it.Metadata.Name)
```

Why it matters: The shipped examples recommend repeating an inline connection block across workflows (workflow-0/1/3 share mq-core, and register() merges each side's passthrough onto the one binder, consolidate.go:177-179). If that repeated block carries a nested additional-properties entry (Prop.Sub != nil), condition 579 is true on every re-registration regardless of content, so each generate reports 'set more than once; last (by filename) wins' for a value that did not change -- warning noise the operator learns to ignore. The inverse case is wrong the other way: a later side that replaces the nested value with an empty scalar (`key:`) has p.Val == list[i].Val == "" and p.Sub == nil, so it is neither applied nor reported. @@ -576,7 +577,7 @@ func QuoteScalar(s string) string {

```diff
 		if list[i].Key == p.Key {
-			if list[i].Val != p.Val || (p.Sub != nil) {
+			if list[i].Val != p.Val || !sameNode(list[i].Sub, p.Sub) {

@@ -586,6 +587,19 @@ func mergeProp(list []Prop, p Prop, warns *[]string, binder string) []Prop {
 	return append(list, p)
 }
 
+// sameNode reports whether two verbatim subtrees would render identically:
+// nil equals only nil, and two nodes are compared by their encoding, so a
+// nested passthrough block repeated on another side is one value, not a
+// change.
+func sameNode(a, b *yaml.Node) bool {
+	if a == nil || b == nil {
+		return a == b
+	}
+	x, errA := yaml.Marshal(a)
+	y, errB := yaml.Marshal(b)
+	return errA == nil && errB == nil && bytes.Equal(x, y)
+}
```

#### CR-0147 [minor] [new] validateFilenameShape passes C1 controls and Windows-reserved characters

Location: internal/libs/libs.go:564-586, internal/libs/libs.go:481
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    571:	if strings.ContainsAny(name, "/\\") {
    572:		return fmt.Errorf("filename %q contains a path separator", name)
    573:	}
    574:	if filepath.IsAbs(name) {
    577:	for _, r := range name {
    578:		if r < 0x20 || r == 0x7f {
    579:			return fmt.Errorf("filename %q contains a control character", name)
    481:		dst := filepath.Join(in.Dir, name)

Why it matters: The name is decoded from the URL's last segment, so an operator-supplied or redirect-supplied URL controls it byte for byte. Line 578 rejects C0 and DEL only: U+0080-U+009F (C1 controls, e.g. %C2%85) pass. Nothing rejects `<>:"|?*`, and on the Windows build (a release target in tag.yml) a decoded `C:x.jar` is drive-relative -- filepath.IsAbs is false -- so Join yields `libs\C:x.jar`, which NTFS treats as an alternate data stream of a file `C`; the rename either fails with an opaque error or creates a stream no classpath will see while Report.Written claims the jar. The lane doc (libs.go:5-6) promises the filename is 'validated only after decoding'; the validation should cover the characters a filesystem rewrites, not only path separators.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/libs/libs.go
+++ b/internal/libs/libs.go
@@ -571,11 +571,17 @@ func validateFilenameShape(name string) error {
 	if strings.ContainsAny(name, "/\\") {
 		return fmt.Errorf("filename %q contains a path separator", name)
 	}
+	// Reserved on Windows, where ':' also opens an NTFS alternate data
+	// stream; the Windows build is a release target, so the shape is the
+	// same on every platform rather than left to the filesystem to reject.
+	if strings.ContainsAny(name, "<>:\"|?*") {
+		return fmt.Errorf("filename %q contains a character a filesystem may reject or rewrite", name)
+	}
 	if filepath.IsAbs(name) {
 		return fmt.Errorf("filename %q is an absolute path", name)
 	}
 	for _, r := range name {
-		if r < 0x20 || r == 0x7f {
+		if r < 0x20 || (r >= 0x7f && r <= 0x9f) {
 			return fmt.Errorf("filename %q contains a control character", name)
 		}
 	}
```

#### CR-0148 [minor] [new] fetchSHA1Sidecar appends .sha1 after a query string or fragment

```diff
+// an explicit --url may carry a query (a token, a pre-signed URL) or a

+func sidecarURL(rawURL string) (string, error) {
```

#### CR-0165 [minor] [new] Block scalar ends early in blockIndicator: no indentation indicator for a leading-space first line

Location: internal/render/render.go:48-53, internal/render/render.go:36-44, internal/render/render.go:57-65, internal/render/render.go:364-372, internal/consolidate/consolidate.go:519-523, internal/render/render_test.go:697-733, internal/render/render.go:36-65
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    internal/render/render.go:
    41 	indicator, body := blockIndicator(val)
    42 	w.Line(indent, key+": "+indicator)
    43 	writeBlockBody(w, indent+2, body)
    48 func blockIndicator(val string) (indicator, body string) {
    49 	if strings.HasSuffix(val, "\n") {
    50 		return "|", strings.TrimSuffix(val, "\n")
    51 	}
    52 	return "|-", val
    63 		w.Line(indent, ln)
    internal/consolidate/consolidate.go:
    519 	case yaml.LiteralStyle, yaml.FoldedStyle:
    520 		if !strings.Contains(n.Value, "\n") {
    523 		return n.Value

Why it matters: FormatScalar returns a multi-line literal/folded source value verbatim (523) and writeScalar re-emits it as `key: |-` followed by the lines at indent+2 (41-43, 63). YAML detects a block scalar's content indentation from its first non-empty line unless an explicit indentation indicator is given; when that first line itself begins with spaces (a source block written with `|2` and an indented first line, e.g. a SpEL expression whose first line is indented), the parser takes the deeper column as the block's indentation, so the next line at indent+2 is shallower, terminates the scalar, and is parsed as a sibling key of `key` -- a key injection into application.yml, or a parse error, depending on its text. Impact is fidelity for the author's own config, hence minor. Fix: emit `|2`/`|2-` when the body's first line starts with a space (every body is written two columns in from its key or dash).

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/render/render.go
+++ b/internal/render/render.go
@@ -48,6 +48,14 @@ func writeScalar(w *yw, indent int, key, val string) {
 func blockIndicator(val string) (indicator, body string) {
-	if strings.HasSuffix(val, "\n") {
-		return "|", strings.TrimSuffix(val, "\n")
-	}
-	return "|-", val
+	indicator, body = "|-", val
+	if strings.HasSuffix(val, "\n") {
+		indicator, body = "|", strings.TrimSuffix(val, "\n")
+	}
+	// A body whose first line starts with a space needs an explicit indentation
+	// indicator: the parser would otherwise take that deeper indent as the
+	// block's own and end the scalar at the next, shallower line. Every body
+	// is written two columns in from its key or dash, hence the 2.
+	if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimLeft(body, "\n"), " ") {
+		indicator = indicator[:1] + "2" + indicator[1:]
+	}
+	return indicator, body
 }
```

      378	func WriteFile(path, content string, mode os.FileMode) error {

```diff
 }
 
-// sameFile compares two absolute paths for identity, case-insensitively on
-// Windows where the filesystem is case-preserving but case-insensitive.
+// sameFile reports whether two absolute paths name one file: by identity when
+// both can be stat'ed (so a symlinked directory still matches), otherwise by
+// string, case-insensitively on Windows where the filesystem is
+// case-preserving but case-insensitive.
 func sameFile(a, b string) bool {
+	if fa, err := os.Stat(a); err == nil {
+		if fb, err := os.Stat(b); err == nil {
+			return os.SameFile(fa, fb)
```

Why it matters: validate checks tls.*.file, libs.dir and podman.base-dir as typed (relative, usually `./certs/x.jks`). gen then prefixes the absolute env directory, which is never checked, and the renderers concatenate the result unquoted. dockergen's own comment asserts the rest of the document 'cannot carry a $' -- false once the spec lives under a directory such as `/home/me/$proj/specs` or `C:\Users\John Doe\specs`: compose interpolates `$proj` (warning, empty) and silently mounts a different source; a `%` in base-dir reaches the podman service's ExecStart where systemd expands specifiers (podmangen.go:88-93 already doubles `%` for Environment= but not for Volume=). #### CR-0220 [minor] [new] Host target detection diverges: dev.ps1 $TOs hardcodes 'windows', dev.sh host_os passes MSYS uname as GOOS

Location: scripts/dev.ps1:63-71, scripts/dev.sh:54-59, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:55-56, cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:447-448
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    scripts/dev.ps1:2-3
    2  # Dev tasks for solmq-conn-util. Behaviourally identical to dev.sh -- same task names,
    3  # same gating, same footer format.
    scripts/dev.ps1:63-69
    63  function Get-HostArch {
    64    switch ($env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE) {
    65      'AMD64' { 'amd64' } 'ARM64' { 'arm64' } default { 'amd64' }
    68  $TOs   = if ($env:TARGET_OS)   { $env:TARGET_OS }   else { 'windows' }
    69  $TArch = if ($env:TARGET_ARCH) { $env:TARGET_ARCH } else { Get-HostArch }
    scripts/dev.sh:54-57
    54  host_os()   { uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'; }
    55  host_arch() { case "$(uname -m)" in x86_64|amd64) echo amd64;; aarch64|arm64) echo arm64;; *) uname -m;; esac; }
    56  T_OS="${TARGET_OS:-$(host_os)}"
    57  T_ARCH="${TARGET_ARCH:-$(host_arch)}"
    docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:55-56
    ... (2 more lines in the finding record)

Why it matters: Contract: 'Unset means build for the host, using the host's own os/arch in the name, so local and CI output are the same shape.' Run './scripts/dev.ps1 build' under pwsh 7 on Linux or macOS (the script only requires 5.1, so pwsh 7 is in scope): $TOs is 'windows', GOOS=windows is exported and dist/solmq-conn-util-windows-amd64.exe is cross-compiled instead of a host binary. Conversely, run './scripts/dev.sh build' from Git Bash or MSYS on Windows: uname -s gives 'mingw64_nt-10.0-...' so GOOS becomes that string and go build fails with an unsupported GOOS/GOARCH pair -- correct output name in neither case. On an unrecognised architecture dev.sh passes the raw uname -m through (fails loudly in go build) while dev.ps1 quietly picks amd64. Both headers and DEVELOPMENT.md:55-56 claim identical host behaviour. Patch gives dev.ps1 a Get-HostOS mirroring uname -s (Desktop edition implies Windows; pwsh exposes $IsWindows/$IsMacOS) and teaches dev.sh's host_os to map the MSYS/Cygwin/MinGW kernel names to windows.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/scripts/dev.ps1
+++ b/scripts/dev.ps1
@@ -66,4 +66,10 @@ function Get-HostArch {
   }
 }
-$TOs   = if ($env:TARGET_OS)   { $env:TARGET_OS }   else { 'windows' }
+# Host OS, mirroring dev.sh's uname -s mapping: Windows PowerShell (Desktop
+# edition) exists only on Windows; pwsh 7 exposes $IsWindows/$IsMacOS/$IsLinux.
+function Get-HostOS {
+  if ($PSVersionTable.PSEdition -ne 'Core' -or $IsWindows) { 'windows' }
+  elseif ($IsMacOS) { 'darwin' } else { 'linux' }
+}
+$TOs   = if ($env:TARGET_OS)   { $env:TARGET_OS }   else { Get-HostOS }
 $TArch = if ($env:TARGET_ARCH) { $env:TARGET_ARCH } else { Get-HostArch }
--- a/scripts/dev.sh
+++ b/scripts/dev.sh
@@ -54 +54,4 @@
-host_os()   { uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'; }
+host_os() {
+  local s; s=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
+  case "$s" in mingw*|msys*|cygwin*) echo windows;; *) echo "$s";; esac
+}
```

    744:	defer cancel()

    // bcprov-jdk18on at roughly 8.9 MB, so 32 MiB leaves headroom

Why it matters: Both http.Client.Timeout (line 518) and the per-artifact context (line 743) cover the full body read, so an artifact must arrive within 30s end to end: the 32 MiB cap needs a sustained >= 1.1 MB/s, and today's 8.9 MB bcprov needs >= 300 KB/s. On a throttled VPN, hotel wifi or a mobile hotspot the jar fails every time with 'requesting ...: context deadline exceeded', a retry starts from zero (no resume), and Input exposes no timeout. The result is reported (not silent), but there is no workaround short of fetching the jar by other means and placing it manually. A size-aware budget (e.g. a floor plus seconds per MiB of Content-Length), an idle timeout instead of a total one, or an Input.Timeout plumbed from a flag would each fix it; the comment at 116-119 justifies a single deadline against redirect chains, which an idle timeout also satisfies.

    171 	cmd := exec.Command(resolved, c.Argv[1:]...)
    177 	runErr := cmd.Run()

    836 		// sequential actuator calls inside each one.
    838 		out, err := runner.RunStatusScript(c.r, c.cmdArgv, c.platform, inst.Name, inst.Namespace, statusscript.ContainerPath)

Why it matters: Neither wget invocation passes -T; busybox wget's default network timeout is 900 s. OS.Run has no context, deadline or WaitDelay (only Stream sets one). A connector whose management port accepts TCP connections but never answers -- a JVM in a long GC pause, an exhausted Tomcat pool, a deadlocked actuator -- blocks each of the seven get() calls for up to 15 min, so 'status application' hangs for up to ~105 min per instance with only the spinner moving, and a --watch tick (renderOnce is synchronous) stalls the same way. In --health mode the engine masks this by killing the check after HealthTimeoutSeconds (10 s) / timeoutSeconds: 5 -- the one path with no bound is the diagnostic an operator reaches for when the connector misbehaves. Fix: pass a short -T on both wget calls (busybox supports -T SEC), spelled from a shared constant next to HealthTimeoutSeconds so the engine timeout and the in-script timeout cannot drift; a few seconds is already what the engines allow.

Why it matters: Stream's child is ended only through ctx (runner.go:236-251), and ctx is cancelled only when the stop channel fires, which is registered for os.Interrupt alone (logs.go:288). Any other terminating signal -- `kill <pid>` from an operator, a service manager or job runner stopping the wrapper, a SIGHUP from a closed session -- hits Go's default disposition: the parent exits immediately, cancel() never runs, and the `kubectl logs -f` / `docker logs -f` child keeps running against the inherited stdout/stderr (a terminal that now belongs to someone else, or a redirected file that keeps growing) until the platform ends it. Ctrl-C works only because the terminal signals the whole foreground group, so the child gets its own SIGINT. The lead's other half is not a defect: the Interrupt-then-Kill fallback at 245-251 is deliberate and documented (DEVELOPMENT.md:237-238) for Windows, where os.Interrupt is the only deliverable signal anyway. watchStatus (status.go:921) has the same registration; there the cost is only a lost final newline, so the follow path is the one that matters. syscall.SIGTERM is defined on every Go target including windows, so the diff below compiles for both CI runners; add the same signal to status.go:921 and cover it with a test that sends SIGTERM to the test process group under !windows (TestOSStreamDeliversOutputBeforeExitAndCancelIsCleanEnd already proves the cancel side).

Why it matters: podmanDeploy writes up to four files into two directories (base-dir and a quadlet directory derived from the uid) and prints nothing about any of them; the only output is systemctl's. #### CR-0125 [minor] [new] Liveness probe restarts a slow-starting JVM after ~75s while the engine healthchecks wait 150s and never kill; no startupProbe

Location: internal/deploy/deploy.go:443-450, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:54-59
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    internal/deploy/deploy.go:446-450
      w.Line(10, "livenessProbe:")
      w.Line(12, "tcpSocket:")
      w.Line(14, "port: "+strconv.Itoa(mgmtPort))
      w.Line(12, "initialDelaySeconds: 30")
      w.Line(12, "periodSeconds: 15")      // failureThreshold left at the default 3
    internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:55-58 HealthIntervalSeconds 30, HealthTimeoutSeconds 10, HealthRetries 3, HealthStartPeriodSeconds 60 -- "The start period is generous because it covers JVM startup plus the connector's own bindings".

Why it matters: The compose and quadlet checks give the JVM 60s before counting failures and three 30s intervals after that, and even then only report. On kubernetes the actuator port must be open within 30s + 3 x 15s = 75s or kubelet kills the container -- on a cpu: "1" guaranteed pod loading up to 20 workflows plus TLS bundles that is a plausible cold start, and each restart starts the clock again, so a pod that would have come up in 90s never does. The comment at 443-445 justifies tcpSocket over the health check but not the budget. The standard remedy is a startupProbe on the same port that holds liveness off until the port answers (patch: 30 x 10s = 300s ceiling, then liveness takes over unchanged).

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/deploy/deploy.go
+++ b/internal/deploy/deploy.go
@@ -440,6 +440,14 @@ func renderDeployment(w *yw, in Input, inst Instance, ns, credRef, storeRef string, hasStores bo
 	w.Line(14, "mountPath: "+statusscript.ContainerPath)
 	w.Line(14, "subPath: status")
 	w.Line(14, "readOnly: true")
+	// A startup probe holds liveness off until the actuator port opens, so a
+	// slow JVM start is waited for rather than restarted -- the kubernetes
+	// counterpart of the engines' start_period.
+	w.Line(10, "startupProbe:")
+	w.Line(12, "tcpSocket:")
+	w.Line(14, "port: "+strconv.Itoa(mgmtPort))
+	w.Line(12, "periodSeconds: 10")
+	w.Line(12, "failureThreshold: 30")
 	// Liveness stays a tcpSocket probe: it decides whether kubelet restarts the
 	// container, and a connector whose downstream is slow or flapping must not
 	// be restarted for it -- "the actuator port answers" is the right bar.
```

Why it matters: Cleanup is a defer, so it runs on every error return but not when the process dies: Ctrl-C during a 9 MB bcprov leaves a partial `.libs-download-123456.tmp` (0600) in ./libs, the directory that is bind-mounted into the container as the classpath. Nothing in Download removes stale temp files on the next run, and no signal handler exists (the Go checklist asks for signal.NotifyContext or equivalent). Why it matters: The leniency the doc promises for an explicit --url hinges on the host answering exactly 404 for a missing key. #### CR-0158 [minor] [new] fetchXML carries no context deadline and cannot follow a redirect, unlike downloadOne

Location: internal/libs/maven.go:696-717, internal/libs/libs.go:760-787
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    maven.go:
    697:	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, rawURL, nil)
    706:	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
    707:		return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetching %s: unexpected status %d", redactURL(rawURL), resp.StatusCode)
    libs.go:
    760:		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, u, nil)
    769:		if isRedirectStatus(resp.StatusCode) {
    784:		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
    786:			return fmt.Errorf("unexpected status %s from %s", resp.Status, sanitizeURL(parsed))

Why it matters: The three network paths in one package follow different conventions. fetchXML relies on http.Client.Timeout for its bound (none at all with an injected Doer that is not *http.Client), while the jar and sidecar fetches carry an explicit context; the default client's CheckRedirect returns ErrUseLastResponse, so a 301 on maven-metadata.xml or a .pom surfaces as 'unexpected status 301' (the metadata path cannot follow a redirect even though the jar path can), and the status is printed as a bare number where the other paths print resp.Status. None of this breaks today against repo1.maven.org, but the Go checklist asks that the context 'actually reaches the blocking call', and the next change (a mirror base, a CDN redirect on Central) would hit the metadata path first. The patch adds the deadline; redirect handling would reuse the hop loop.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/libs/maven.go
+++ b/internal/libs/maven.go
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@

 import (
+	"context"
 	"encoding/xml"
 	"fmt"
 	"io"
@@ -694,7 +695,9 @@ func jarURL(a artifact) string {
 // fetchXML issues an https GET through d and returns the body, capped at
 // maxXMLBytes read from the wire (never trusting Content-Length).
 func fetchXML(d Doer, rawURL string) ([]byte, error) {
-	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, rawURL, nil)
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), defaultTimeout)
+	defer cancel()
+	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, rawURL, nil)
 	if err != nil {
 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("building request for %s: %w", redactURL(rawURL), err)
```

#### CR-0168 [minor] [new] PodmanRemove aborts on a failed stop before removing the unit, so remove orphans it and cannot be re-run

Location: internal/runner/runner.go:618-638, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:678-702, internal/runner/runner_test.go:467-479, internal/podmangen/podmangen.go:211-212, internal/runner/runner.go:393-404
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    runner.go:620-631
      620     for _, s := range services {
      621         o, err := r.Run(Cmd{Argv: sc.systemctlArgs("stop", s)})
      623         if err != nil {
      624             return out.String(), fmt.Errorf("systemctl stop %s: %w", s, err)
      627     for _, u := range units {
      628         if err := os.Remove(filepath.Join(sc.Dir, u)); ...
    main.go:679-696: podmanRemove continues past a PodmanRemove error to delete base-dir files and run PodmanSecretRemove.
    runner_test.go:467-479 pins the early return.
    runner.go:402: argv = append(argv, verb, "-f", "-")  (kubectl delete without --ignore-not-found)

Why it matters: `systemctl stop <unit>` fails (exit 5, 'Unit ... not loaded') for a unit the generator never produced -- after a deploy whose `daemon-reload` failed (no user bus), after a previous successful remove, or after an operator's own cleanup. PodmanRemove then returns before os.Remove(unit) and before daemon-reload, while podmanRemove goes on to delete application.yml, the status script and every secret. Result: the .container file stays in ~/.config/containers/systemd referencing secrets and mounts that no longer exist, and the next login or daemon-reload lets quadlet generate and try to start it. The second `remove` fails the same way, so the operator cannot converge with the tool. Platform parity: docker `compose down` on an absent stack exits 0, kubernetes `delete -f -` on absent objects exits 1 (no --ignore-not-found), podman fails at stop -- three different answers to 'remove twice'. Fix: record the stop error, still remove the unit files and reload, and return the recorded error at the end.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/runner/runner.go
+++ b/internal/runner/runner.go
@@ -618,11 +618,15 @@

+	var stopErr error
 	for _, s := range services {
 		o, err := r.Run(Cmd{Argv: sc.systemctlArgs("stop", s)})
 		out.WriteString(o)
-		if err != nil {
-			return out.String(), fmt.Errorf("systemctl stop %s: %w", s, err)
+		if err != nil && stopErr == nil {
+			// Keep going: a unit systemd never loaded (a failed deploy, a second
+			// remove) still has to come out of the quadlet directory, or the next
+			// daemon-reload resurrects it.
+			stopErr = fmt.Errorf("systemctl stop %s: %w", s, err)
 		}
 	}
 	for _, u := range units {
@@ -634,5 +638,5 @@
 	if err != nil {
 		return out.String(), fmt.Errorf("systemctl daemon-reload: %w", err)
 	}
-	return out.String(), nil
+	return out.String(), stopErr
 }
```

#### CR-0188 [minor] [new] The EXIT trap is installed before the --health branch clears it, so an abort during config/password resolution in health mode exits 0 (healthy)

Location: internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:108-112, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:289-290, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:134-211
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    statusscript.go
    110 # EXIT trap keeps the 0 contract even if set -u aborts on an unguarded name.
    111 set -u
    112 trap 'exit 0' EXIT
    134 config_files() {
    167 CONFIGS=$(config_files)
    200 PASS=$(from_configs ...)
    289 if [ "${1:-}" = "--health" ]; then
    290   trap - EXIT
    291   H=$(get "$BASE/health" | health_status)

Why it matters: Lines 134-211 (config search, sed over every config, secret file read) run before the --health branch at 289 while the 'exit 0' trap from line 112 is active. The trap exists, per its own comment, because the author expects set -u to be able to abort on an unguarded name; in health mode such an abort (or any future bug in that region) fires the trap and the engine reads exit 0 with no output as a healthy container -- the inverse of a safe default, and the same inversion TestRenderHealthModeExitsOnVerdict guards against for the branch itself ('without that, every container reports healthy forever'). Today every name in that region is guarded, so this is latent rather than live; the fix is to install the trap only for the report path (patch), which keeps 'trap - EXIT' in the branch as a harmless no-op so the existing tests still hold.

```diff
 # EXIT trap keeps the 0 contract even if set -u aborts on an unguarded name.
+# The healthcheck must not inherit that trap: an abort in the config search
+# below would otherwise exit 0 and read as healthy, so it is installed only
+# for the report.
```

#### CR-0219 [minor] [new] Caller session mutated by dev.ps1: Set-Location, NO_COLOR and Task-build env edits are never restored

Location: scripts/dev.ps1:16-17, scripts/dev.ps1:84-88, scripts/dev.ps1:193-205, scripts/dev.sh:14-16, scripts/dev.sh:72-73, scripts/dev.ps1:84-87
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    dev.ps1:16  Set-Location $RepoRoot
    dev.ps1:17  $env:NO_COLOR = '1'
    dev.ps1:84    $env:CGO_ENABLED = '0'; $env:GOOS = $TOs; $env:GOARCH = $TArch
    dev.ps1:85    $code = Invoke-Logged 'build' 'go' @(
    dev.ps1:87    Remove-Item Env:CGO_ENABLED, Env:GOOS, Env:GOARCH -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    dev.sh:14   cd "$REPO_ROOT"
    dev.sh:16   export NO_COLOR=1
    dev.sh:72     run build env CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$T_OS" GOARCH="$T_ARCH" \
    dev.sh:73       go build -trimpath -ldflags ...
    Contract: "Works from any cwd: the script resolves its own location and `cd`s to the repo root."

Why it matters: dev.sh runs in its own process, so `cd` and `export` die with it, and GOOS/GOARCH/CGO_ENABLED are scoped to the one child via `env`. dev.ps1 runs inside the caller's PowerShell process: Set-Location (line 16) changes the interactive session's current directory for good, `$env:NO_COLOR` (line 17) stays set in the session, and Task-build (line 87) deletes CGO_ENABLED/GOOS/GOARCH outright rather than restoring the values a developer may have exported for other work (a cross-compile shell, cgo projects). If Invoke-Logged throws, the dispatcher's catch (line 199) runs with the three variables still set, so the next task or the next `go` command in that session builds for the wrong target. Behaviourally identical means a developer running `.\scripts\dev.ps1 build` from a subfolder should end exactly where dev.sh leaves them. Fix: Push-Location/Pop-Location around the dispatch, save and restore the three env vars in a try/finally inside Task-build, and set NO_COLOR only for the duration (restore the prior value on exit, including the Die path).

#### CR-0013 [major] [new] defaultClient() redirect policy and timeout have no test; every test injects a fake Doer

Location: internal/libs/libs.go:512-523, internal/libs/libs_test.go:115-121
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    libs.go:516-522
    516  func defaultClient() *http.Client {
    517      return &http.Client{
    518          Timeout: defaultTimeout,
    519          CheckRedirect: func(req *http.Request, via []*http.Request) error {
    520              return http.ErrUseLastResponse
    521          },
    522      }
    libs.go:512-515 (doc): 'CheckRedirect returns http.ErrUseLastResponse so Do never follows a redirect on its own: downloadOne inspects and re-validates every hop itself'
    grep -rn defaultClient internal/ cmd/ -> only libs.go:319 and :516; no *_test.go reference.
    Every Download call in libs_test.go passes HTTP: fd (e.g. :121, :148, :173, :1239, :1324).

Why it matters: The per-hop https re-validation in downloadOne (libs.go:756) and fetchSHA1Sidecar (:663) only runs in production because the stdlib client is told not to follow redirects. If CheckRedirect were removed or changed (a plausible 'simplification'), http.Client would follow a 302 to an http:// host itself and downloadOne would only ever see the final 200 -- the downgrade guard would be bypassed in production while every test, which never constructs the real client, keeps passing. The same holds for Timeout: nothing pins that the production client has one. A three-assertion unit test closes both holes without touching the network.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/libs/libs_test.go
+++ b/internal/libs/libs_test.go
@@ -1363,3 +1363,20 @@ func TestDownloadSyslogWithNoReleaseOnTheLineIsSystemic(t *testing.T) {
 		t.Errorf("dir has %v, want nothing written", entries)
 	}
 }
+
+// TestDefaultClientNeverFollowsRedirectsItself pins the only production Doer:
+// every hop has to come back to downloadOne/fetchSHA1Sidecar for https
+// re-validation, so the client must refuse to follow on its own, and it must
+// carry the package timeout.
+func TestDefaultClientNeverFollowsRedirectsItself(t *testing.T) {
+	c := defaultClient()
+	if c.Timeout != defaultTimeout {
+		t.Errorf("Timeout = %v, want %v", c.Timeout, defaultTimeout)
+	}
+	if c.CheckRedirect == nil {
+		t.Fatal("CheckRedirect is nil: the stdlib client would follow redirects, skipping per-hop https validation")
+	}
+	if err := c.CheckRedirect(nil, nil); err != http.ErrUseLastResponse {
+		t.Errorf("CheckRedirect = %v, want http.ErrUseLastResponse", err)
+	}
+}
```

```diff
diff --git a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands_doc_test.go b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands_doc_test.go

+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/commands_doc_test.go

 		}

 }

+// TestHelpSurfacesArePlainASCII holds every rendering of the model to the same
+// output contract TestCompletionOutputIsPlainASCIILF holds the scripts to --
+// plain ASCII and LF only -- and pins the cliFlag.Usage rules its doc comment
+// states (no backticks, no trailing period): Usage reaches only the terminal
+// pages, which no other gate reads for encoding.
+func TestHelpSurfacesArePlainASCII(t *testing.T) {
+	surfaces := map[string]string{
+		"usage()":      usageText(),
+		"commands.md":  renderCommandsDoc(),
+		"abbreviation": renderAbbreviationDoc(),
+	}
+	for _, v := range cliVerbs {
+		surfaces["help "+v.Name] = verbUsage(v.Name)
+	}
+	for name, text := range surfaces {
+		for i := 0; i < len(text); i++ {
+			if text[i] >= 0x80 {
+				t.Errorf("%s has a non-ASCII byte %#x at offset %d", name, text[i], i)
+				break
+			}
+			if text[i] == '\r' {
+				t.Errorf("%s has a CR at offset %d; output must be LF only", name, i)

+			}

+			t.Errorf("flag %s Usage carries a backtick, which terminal help never renders: %q", f.Long, f.Usage)
+		}
+		if strings.HasSuffix(f.Usage, ".") {

+		}
+	}
+}
```

    docs/test.md:1224: "every spelling flag.Parse accepts (-e, --e, -env, `--env`) is in the value-skipping table, so a value is never mistaken for a positional"
    docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:111-112: "the value kinds (`-e`/`-o` complete a path, `examples` completes a directory) survive into each script"
    ... (3 more lines in the finding record)

Why it matters: flagAliases (completion.go:151-166) yields, for -e/--env, the spellings -e, --e, -env, --env. Each is a substring of --env, and --env is already in every script through the offered-flag lists that TestCompletionCoversModel checks (completion_test.go:149-152); the same holds for every other value-taking flag (-platform within --platform, -o within --out, and so on). strings.Contains(script, alias) at line 295 is therefore true whether or not the alias is in the value-skipping case (_solmq_conn_util_flag_arg, bash golden lines 20-40) or the powershell $flagArg table -- the test cannot fail for the regression it describes, and the catalogue row (test.md:1224) states a guarantee the test does not establish. TestCompletionValueKindsReachScripts likewise checks only that some 'file' construct exists in bash/zsh/fish and pins -e alone in powershell, so the DEVELOPMENT.md:111 claim that -e and -o complete a path in each shell is backed, per flag, only for --omit-lib-file (TestCompletionOmitLibFileCompletesFiles, lines 347-362). A renderer that dropped -o from the table, or mapped it to 'name', would change the golden (reviewable) but fail no semantic test once regenerated. The patch rewrites TestCompletionRecognizesFlagAliases to assert each shell's own table construct for every value-taking flag, carrying its Arg kind, which also covers the per-flag value-kind claim in all four shells (fish through its -r / -r -F selectors).

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion_test.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion_test.go
@@ -281,22 +281,52 @@
-// TestCompletionRecognizesFlagAliases covers the value-skipping table: Go's flag
-// package accepts -env for --env, so a script that only knows the documented
-// spelling would treat the value after -env as a positional and offer targets
-// where a filename belongs. fish is excluded -- its -s/-l model has no alias
-// table and covers the two documented spellings only.
-func TestCompletionRecognizesFlagAliases(t *testing.T) {
-	scripts := renderedCompletions(t)
-	for _, shell := range []string{"bash", "zsh", "powershell"} {
-		t.Run(shell, func(t *testing.T) {
-			for _, f := range completionFlags() {
-				if f.Arg == argNone {
-					continue // consumes no value, so there is nothing to skip
-				}
-				for _, alias := range f.Aliases {
-					if !strings.Contains(scripts[shell], alias) {
-						t.Errorf("%s completion does not recognize flag spelling %q", shell, alias)
-					}
-				}
-			}
-		})
-	}
-}
+// TestCompletionRecognizesFlagAliases covers the value-skipping table: Go's flag
+// package accepts -env for --env, so a script that only knows the documented
+// spelling would treat the value after -env as a positional and offer targets
+// where a filename belongs. Each shell's own table construct is asserted per
+// flag, carrying the flag's value kind, so a flag missing from the table or
+// wired to the wrong kind fails by name -- a bare substring search cannot,
+// since every alias is a substring of the long spelling the offer lists
+// already carry. fish has no alias table; its -s/-l spec is asserted with the
+// -r/-F selectors its value kind requires.
+func TestCompletionRecognizesFlagAliases(t *testing.T) {
+	scripts := renderedCompletions(t)
+	table := map[string]func(f completionFlag) []string{
+		"bash": func(f completionFlag) []string {
+			return []string{"    " + strings.Join(f.Aliases, "|") + ") printf '" + f.Arg + "' ;;"}
+		},
+		"zsh": func(f completionFlag) []string {
+			return []string{"    " + strings.Join(f.Aliases, "|") + ") print -n '" + f.Arg + "' ;;"}
+		},
+		"powershell": func(f completionFlag) []string {
+			var out []string
+			for _, a := range f.Aliases {
+				out = append(out, "    $flagArg['"+a+"'] = '"+f.Arg+"'")
+			}
+			return out
+		},
+		"fish": func(f completionFlag) []string {
+			sel := " -r -d "
+			if f.Arg == argFile {
+				sel = " -r -F -d "
+			}
+			return []string{" " + fishFlagSpec(f) + sel}
+		},
+	}
+	for shell, script := range scripts {
+		t.Run(shell, func(t *testing.T) {
+			want, ok := table[shell]
+			if !ok {
+				t.Fatalf("shell %q has no value-skipping construct; add one when adding a shell", shell)
+			}
+			for _, f := range completionFlags() {
+				if f.Arg == argNone {
+					continue // consumes no value, so there is nothing to skip
+				}
+				for _, line := range want(f) {
+					if !strings.Contains(script, line) {
+						t.Errorf("%s completion does not skip a %s value after %s (want %q)", shell, f.Arg, f.Long, line)
+					}
+				}
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}
```

     157  f, ok := byShort[sh]
     158  if !ok {
     159      continue // TestCompletionModelMetadataComplete reports the broken key
    ... (2 more lines in the finding record)

Why it matters: A verb's Flags list is a list of string keys (commands.go:299, 313, 323, 338, 374, 393, 417, 423, 430) resolved against cliFlags.Short at render time. A key that matches nothing -- a literal typo such as "-E" or "-env" in place of "-e" -- is skipped in three places: completionVerbs (completion.go:97-101), so every completion script omits the flag under that verb; flagEntries (commands.go:784-788), so the verb's help page omits it; and flagsLine (commands.go:504-511), so docs/commands.md's 'Flags:' line omits it while the Flags table's hand-written AppliesTo column still claims the verb. All three sites and TestVerbUsagePages point at TestCompletionModelMetadataComplete as the gate, but that test never reads v.Flags, so nothing fails. The orphan check at commands_doc_test.go:182-194 only catches the case where the misspelt flag is listed by no other verb; '-e' is listed by eight verbs, so a typo in one of them is invisible. The runtime flag sets are registered by hand in each handler (main.go:1192-1203, status.go:149-172), so the effect is documentation and completion drift rather than a rejected flag -- the exact drift the model exists to prevent. The patch adds the missing loop.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion_test.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion_test.go
@@ -447,5 +447,9 @@ func TestCompletionModelMetadataComplete(t *testing.T) {
 	knownPosArgs := map[string]bool{posNone: true, posDir: true}
 	knownArgs := map[string]bool{argNone: true, argFile: true, argName: true}
+	flagByShort := make(map[string]bool, len(cliFlags))
+	for _, f := range cliFlags {
+		flagByShort[f.Short] = true
+	}
 
 	// Collides with a verb name, another alias, or -h/--help would make dispatch's
 	// alias resolution (or a shell's own $verb-normalization case) ambiguous.
@@ -464,4 +468,12 @@ func TestCompletionModelMetadataComplete(t *testing.T) {
 		if !knownPosArgs[v.PosArg] {
 			t.Errorf("verb %q declares PosArg %q, which no renderer handles", v.Name, v.PosArg)
 		}
+		// completionVerbs, flagEntries and flagsLine each skip a Flags key that
+		// names no cliFlags.Short and point here as the gate -- this is it.
+		for _, sh := range v.Flags {
+			if !flagByShort[sh] {
+				t.Errorf("verb %q lists flag key %q, which no cliFlags entry declares; the help page, "+
+					"the docs Flags line and every completion script would drop it silently", v.Name, sh)
+			}
+		}
 		assertShellSafeName(t, "verb", v.Name)
```

```diff
+// countTestFuncs counts lines matching testFuncRe across every *_test.go file
+// under root -- the doc's own counting rule.
+func countTestFuncs(root string) (int, error) {
+	total := 0
+	err := walkTestFiles(root, func(b []byte) { total += len(testFuncRe.FindAll(b, -1)) })
 	return total, err
 }
+
+// testFuncNames collects the name of every top-level test function under root.
+func testFuncNames(root string) (map[string]bool, error) {
+	names := map[string]bool{}
+	err := walkTestFiles(root, func(b []byte) {
+		for _, m := range testFuncNameRe.FindAllSubmatch(b, -1) {
+			names[string(m[1])] = true
+		}
+	})
+	return names, err
+}
```

Why it matters: The only resolution test (runner_test.go:742-747) covers a binary that does not exist anywhere; the documented security property -- a same-directory hit is refused even though it exists -- is pinned by no test for Run, RunSplit, Stream or Attach (TestOSStreamRejectsEmptyAndUnresolvableArgv, TestOSAttachRejectsEmptyAndUnresolvableArgv and TestOSRunSplitRejectsEmptyAndUnresolvableArgv all reuse the not-found name). (which resolves lazily and, through its own ErrDot handling, would still refuse) or a GODEBUG=execerrdot=0 in a build environment, or a change that strips the error check at 321-326, would pass the suite unchanged. Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/runner/runner_test.go
+++ b/internal/runner/runner_test.go
@@ -3,8 +3,10 @@ package runner
 import (
 	"context"
+	"errors"
 	"fmt"
 	"io"
 	"os"
+	"os/exec"
 	"path/filepath"
 	"reflect"

 	}
 }
 
+// TestOSRunRefusesACurrentDirectoryResolution pins the exec.ErrDot refusal the
+// Run doc comment and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md promise: a binary that resolves only
+// through the current directory is refused before anything is started.
+func TestOSRunRefusesACurrentDirectoryResolution(t *testing.T) {
+	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
+		t.Skip("windows consults the current directory by default; the unix PATH form of this test does not transfer")
+	}
+	dir := t.TempDir()
+	const name = "solmq-errdot-probe"
+	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, name), []byte("#!/bin/sh\necho ran\n"), 0o755); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	t.Chdir(dir)
+	t.Setenv("PATH", ".")
+	out, err := (OS{}).Run(Cmd{Argv: []string{name}})
+	if !errors.Is(err, exec.ErrDot) {
+		t.Fatalf("Run = (%q, %v), want an error wrapping exec.ErrDot", out, err)
+	}
+	if out != "" {
+		t.Errorf("nothing may run when argv[0] resolves through the current directory, got %q", out)
+	}
+}
```

```diff
+			}
```

Why it matters: The outer branch at tls.go:207 decides whether a binder is mTLS. Its negative -- a keystore IS configured in tls: but this binder has no key alias -- is the common shape (one shared keystore, only some Solace connections using mTLS), and it is what keeps SSL_KEY_STORE, SSL_KEY_STORE_PASSWORD and the keystore password placeholder (a mounted secret) out of a connection that must not present a client certificate. The patch adds the missing case; it also pins that secretRef is called for the truststore only, so a regression that records the keystore password for a non-mTLS binder is caught.
```diff
--- a/internal/tls/tls_test.go
+++ b/internal/tls/tls_test.go
@@ -143,3 +143,26 @@
```
