 }
+
+// A binder with no key alias is plain TLS, not mTLS: a configured keystore must
+// not reach its api-properties, and its password must not be recorded as a
+// mounted secret for it.
+func TestSolacePropsNoAliasEmitsNoKeystore(t *testing.T) {
+	d := &spec.Defaults{TLS: spec.TLSConfig{
+		Truststore: &spec.Store{File: "./certs/truststore.jks", PasswordEnv: "TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD_ENV", Type: "JKS"},
+		Keystore:   &spec.Store{File: "./certs/keystore.jks", Password: "s3cr3t-literal", Type: "JKS"},
+	}}
+	var stables []string
+	rec := func(stable string, c spec.Cred) string {
+		stables = append(stables, stable)
+		return "${" + stable + "}"
+	}
+	for _, kv := range SolaceProps(d, "", true, rec) {
+		if strings.HasPrefix(kv.Key, "SSL_KEY_STORE") || kv.Key == "SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_ALIAS" {
+			t.Errorf("no key alias, but SolaceProps emitted %s=%q", kv.Key, kv.Val)
+		}
+	}
+	if len(stables) != 1 || stables[0] != TruststorePasswordName {
+		t.Errorf("secretRef stable names = %v, want [%s] only", stables, TruststorePasswordName)
+	}
+}

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:297-313, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:3158-3161, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:3646-3658, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:3665-3694, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:3747-3777, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:3875-3896, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:3902-3937, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:3943-4007, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:4015-4082, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:4180-4199, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:4220-4272
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    main_test.go:300 // "fail from index N onward". Calls beyond len(resp) succeed with no output.
    main_test.go:309-312:
    309 	if idx < len(q.resp) {
    310 		return q.resp[idx].out, q.resp[idx].err
    311 	}
    312 	return "", nil
    main_test.go:3158-3161:
    3158 // The engine queries are asserted by their argv and their COUNT: one call for
    3159 // many instances is the whole cost argument for collecting engine facts by
    3160 // default, and a regression to one call per instance would pass every content
    3161 // assertion while quietly multiplying the cost.
    Tests in 3646-4272 listed in locations build a queueRunner and never assert len(q.calls).

Why it matters: The double answers every call past its script with ("", nil), and eleven of the status tests in this range assert only on stdout/stderr. The section header promises that call counts are asserted so a one-call-per-instance regression cannot pass, but only the tests that happen to check len(q.calls) deliver that; in the others an added query (a second inspect per instance, a repeated get, an extra systemctl read) consumes an empty success and the content assertions still hold. Attaching the test to the double and reporting any unscripted call makes the stated contract hold for every case that scripted its calls, without touching the tests themselves (cases that intentionally rely on the permissive tail can leave t nil).

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go
@@ -297,17 +297,23 @@ type queuedResp struct {
 // queueRunner is a fakeRunner variant status's tests need: each call in a
 // sequence returns its own (out, err) pair (e.g. probe-absent, then
 // install-succeeds, then run-standby) rather than fakeRunner's uniform
-// "fail from index N onward". Calls beyond len(resp) succeed with no output.
+// "fail from index N onward". Calls beyond len(resp) succeed with no output,
+// and are reported through t when one is attached, so a case that scripted
+// every call it expects cannot be passed by an extra, unplanned query.
 type queueRunner struct {
 	calls []fakeCall
 	resp  []queuedResp
+	t     *testing.T
 }
 
 func (q *queueRunner) Run(c runner.Cmd) (string, error) {
 	idx := len(q.calls)
 	q.calls = append(q.calls, fakeCall{argv: c.Argv, stdin: c.Stdin, env: c.Env})
 	if idx < len(q.resp) {
 		return q.resp[idx].out, q.resp[idx].err
 	}
+	if q.t != nil {
+		q.t.Errorf("unscripted runner call %d: %v", idx, c.Argv)
+	}
 	return "", nil
 }

#### CR-0002 [major] [new] CI never gates code changes: no push/PR trigger for Go sources and no schedule for the scanner

Location: .github/workflows/ci.yml:12-24, .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-5, .github/dependabot.yml:8-9, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:172-175, .github/dependabot.yml:8-12, scripts/dev.sh:128-130, go.mod:7-18, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:186-187, .github/workflows/ci.yml:19-24
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    ci.yml:3-5   # No automatic triggers by design: nothing runs on push or PR. The full stack
                 # runs once, on a tag, via tag.yml. `workflow_dispatch` is here so you can
                 # still fire a manual run from the Actions tab without pushing a commit.
    ci.yml:12-24 on:
                   workflow_call:
                   workflow_dispatch:
                   pull_request:
                     paths:
                       - ".github/workflows/**"
                       - ".github/dependabot.yml"
                       - "scripts/dev.sh"
                       - "scripts/dev.ps1"
    dependabot.yml:9  - package-ecosystem: github-actions   (the only ecosystem)
    DEVELOPMENT.md:173 Nothing runs on a normal push or PR; it fires when `tag.yml` calls it, on
    DEVELOPMENT.md:174 manual dispatch, and on PRs that touch CI config or the dev scripts

Why it matters: This is documented and deliberate, so judge it by impact. (1) Every commit or PR that changes *.go, go.mod or go.sum reaches main with zero verification: build, vet, test and govulncheck run only when someone pushes a v* tag or clicks workflow_dispatch. A broken main is discovered at release time, when the fix competes with the release. (2) The vulnerability scan the project relies on (scan = go tool govulncheck, dev.sh:128-130) has no schedule: a vulnerability disclosed in gopkg.in/yaml.v3, golang.org/x/* or the Go standard library after the last tag is not seen until the next tag, and the published release binaries stay unflagged meanwhile. The checklist treats a dependency scan that does not run on the right triggers as a blocker-class gap; because the gate does block whenever it runs, this is filed as major. (3) The pull_request path filter is justified in ci.yml:15-18 as what stops Dependabot bumps from 'merging with zero verification', but Dependabot is configured for github-actions only (dependabot.yml:9); the deliberate manual go.mod bumps that DEVELOPMENT.md:180-181 describes (govulncheck, toolchain) are exactly the PRs the filter does not cover. The minimal fix that respects the 'tag is the pipeline' design is a weekly schedule so the scanner stays current, plus go.mod/go.sum in the PR path filter so a pin bump is gated like an action bump.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/.github/workflows/ci.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
@@ -12,6 +12,10 @@
 on:
   workflow_call:
   workflow_dispatch:
+  # Weekly: govulncheck is only as current as its last run, and nothing else
+  # runs between tags. A hit here is the signal to bump and re-tag.
+  schedule:
+    - cron: "17 3 * * 1"
   # Deliberately narrow. Nothing runs on a normal push or PR, but a PR that
   # touches CI config gets the full gate -- which is what validates Dependabot's
   # action bumps. Without this they would merge with zero verification, since
@@ -22,6 +26,8 @@
       - ".github/dependabot.yml"
       - "scripts/dev.sh"
       - "scripts/dev.ps1"
+      - "go.mod"
+      - "go.sum"
 
 permissions:
   contents: read
```

#### CR-0033 [minor] [new] Release binaries are unsigned and unattested; SHA256SUMS is produced by the same job that uploads it

Location: .github/workflows/tag.yml:99-103, .github/workflows/tag.yml:152-153, .github/workflows/tag.yml:210-272, .github/workflows/tag.yml:250-273, .github/workflows/tag.yml:210-223
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    .github/workflows/tag.yml
      221	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04 # pinned; see ci.yml
      222	    permissions:
      223	      contents: write # the only job that can write to the repo
      252	        if [ -d dist ] && [ -n "$(ls -A dist 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
      253	          ( cd dist && sha256sum -- * > ../SHA256SUMS.txt )
      254	          mv SHA256SUMS.txt dist/
      268	        gh release create "$TAG" \
      269	          --verify-tag \
      272	          $(ls -1 dist/* 2>/dev/null || true)
      (id-token: write / attestations: write are granted only to the image job, lines 99-103, which this project never runs: there is no Dockerfile)

Why it matters: The binaries job cross-compiles with CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath and the release job publishes them with a SHA256SUMS.txt computed in that same job from the downloaded artifacts. A checksum generated beside the artifact by the publisher detects download corruption only; anyone able to replace a release asset can regenerate the sums, and nothing ties the binaries to this workflow run or this commit. The image path already asks for provenance and SBOM attestations (tag.yml:152-153) but the binaries path, the only one this repo exercises, gets none. Fix: in the release job add `id-token: write` and `attestations: write` and run a SHA-pinned actions/attest-build-provenance step over dist/* before `gh release create` (or sign SHA256SUMS.txt with cosign sign-blob keyless), and mention `gh attestation verify` in the README install section. Not patched because the action SHA has to be looked up and pinned per the house rule.

    128  $total = (go tool cover "-func=coverage.out" | Select-Object -Last 1)
    129  Add-Content -Path (Get-Log 'cov') -Value $total -Encoding utf8
    130  Write-Host $total
    131  return 0
    scripts/dev.sh
    7    set -uo pipefail
    115  go tool cover -html=coverage.out -o coverage.html
    116  go tool cover -func=coverage.out | tail -n1 | tee -a "$LOG_DIR/cov.log"
    dev.sh:3 "Keep dev.ps1 behaviourally identical."

Why it matters: Task-cov checks only the go test exit code (126). Lines 127 and 128 run the two cover steps without reading $LASTEXITCODE and line 131 returns 0 unconditionally, so when coverage.out is unreadable or coverage.html cannot be written (read-only tree, disk full, a Windows file lock) the footer still records 'cov | OK' and the log carries no total line -- the floor the S5 rule depends on is silently absent. In dev.sh the -func pipeline at 116 is the function's last command, so pipefail (7) makes a -func failure the task's exit code, but 115 (-html) is unchecked in both scripts. cov is local-only (not in `all`, never in CI), so impact is a misleading local footer; the broken rule is the mirrored-behaviour contract.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/scripts/dev.ps1
+++ b/scripts/dev.ps1
@@ -125,7 +125,9 @@ function Task-cov {
   $code = Invoke-Logged 'cov' 'go' @('test','-coverpkg=./...','-coverprofile=coverage.out','-count=1','./...')
   if ($code -ne 0) { return $code }
-  go tool cover "-html=coverage.out" -o coverage.html | Out-Null
+  $code = Invoke-Logged 'cov' 'go' @('tool','cover','-html=coverage.out','-o','coverage.html')
+  if ($code -ne 0) { return $code }
   $total = (go tool cover "-func=coverage.out" | Select-Object -Last 1)
+  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { return $LASTEXITCODE }
   Add-Content -Path (Get-Log 'cov') -Value $total -Encoding utf8
   Write-Host $total
   return 0
--- a/scripts/dev.sh
+++ b/scripts/dev.sh
@@ -112,6 +112,6 @@ task_cov() {
   # tests); without it those lines report 0% and the floor lies. Adding it is
   # a one-time step change in the total -- the floor resets at that run.
   run cov go test -coverpkg=./... -coverprofile=coverage.out -count=1 ./... || return $?
-  go tool cover -html=coverage.out -o coverage.html
+  go tool cover -html=coverage.out -o coverage.html || return $?
   go tool cover -func=coverage.out | tail -n1 | tee -a "$LOG_DIR/cov.log"

    .github/workflows/ci.yml:52,71: the gates workflow uses only actions/checkout and actions/upload-artifact
    .github/workflows/tag.yml:229  - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1

Why it matters: A Dependabot PR bumping actions/download-artifact edits tag.yml, which matches the paths filter, so ci.yml runs -- but ci.yml never invokes download-artifact. The failure surfaces only on the next tag push, inside the release job after plan, gates and binaries have run, and it blocks that release until a fix is tagged. Fail-safe, so impact is low; but 'safe' and 'full gate' in the comment describe more coverage than exists, and a maintainer enabling auto-merge on that promise will be surprised at release time. #### CR-0011 [major] [new] libs-download initContainer in renderDeployment fetches jars with no TLS validation or checksum

Location: internal/deploy/deploy.go:358-371, internal/spec/kubernetes.go:394-396, internal/validate/validate.go:839-851, docs/userguide.md:1346, internal/validate/validate.go:855-863, internal/deploy/deploy.go:357-371, internal/libs/libs.go:526-531
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    internal/deploy/deploy.go:
    360 		cmds := make([]string, 0, len(d.URLs))
    361 		for _, u := range d.URLs {
    362 			cmds = append(cmds, "wget -O '/libs/"+spec.BaseName(u)+"' '"+u+"'")
    363 		}
    366 		w.Line(10, "image: "+d.Image)
    367 		w.Line(10, `command: ["sh", "-c", `+strconv.Quote(strings.Join(cmds, " && "))+`]`)
    internal/spec/kubernetes.go:
    394 		if lb.Download != nil && lb.Download.Image == "" {
    395 			lb.Download.Image = "busybox:1.37"
    internal/validate/validate.go:844-847 checks only safeLibsURL (scheme + charset).
    docs/userguide.md:1346: "an initContainer `wget`s each URL into `/libs` at pod start"

Why it matters: The jars fetched here are loaded by the connector JVM (the libs dir is on the image's classpath), so whoever controls the download controls code execution in the connector. The generated command fetches with busybox's wget, which in the busybox image performs TLS without certificate validation (it prints 'TLS certificate validation not implemented' and proceeds), and the command carries no checksum or digest to compare against, so an on-path attacker or a compromised mirror can substitute a jar on every pod start (the volume is an emptyDir unless pvc is set, so the fetch repeats). The project's own `download jar` verb resolves sha1 sidecars (per the project map), so the two paths disagree about integrity. The default image is a mutable tag (busybox:1.37), not a digest, which S3 also asks for. Smaller gaps in the same block: two URLs with one base name make the second wget overwrite the first, and a URL ending in '/' yields `-O '/libs/'`, which fails the init container -- neither is validated. What would confirm the TLS claim: running `wget -O /dev/null https://example.invalid/` in busybox:1.37 and observing the note, or checking the image's wget build. Suggested fix: accept a per-URL sha256 in the spec and verify it in the command (`sha256sum -c`), or document that only an internal, trusted repository may be listed; pin the image by digest; reject duplicate and empty base names in checkLibs.

    internal/deploy/deploy.go:364-371 initContainers: name, image, command, volumeMounts -- no resources, no securityContext.
    internal/dockergen/dockergen.go:112-130 service: image, container_name, labels, restart, ports -- no privileged:, cap_drop:, security_opt:, user:, read_only:.
    internal/podmangen/podmangen.go:138-143 [Container]: Image=, ContainerName=, Label= -- no DropCapability=, NoNewPrivileges=, User=, ReadOnly=.
    internal/deploy/deploy.go:479-484 secret volume `defaultMode: 0400` with no fsGroup/runAsUser anywhere; cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:660 writes the podman application.yml 0600.
    Repo-wide grep over *.go/*.yaml/*.yml/*.md/*.html for privileged|cap_drop|DropCapability|no-new-privileges|NoNewPrivileges|allowPrivilegeEscalation|read_only|ReadOnly=|readOnlyRootFilesystem|runAsUser|runAsGroup|fsGroup|runAsNonRoot|securityContext|seccomp|network_mode|Network=|hostNetwork: no hit in any source or golden (only validate tests that inject the word 'privileged' to prove rejection, and userguide.md:1728 naming fsGroup as a hazard).

Why it matters: House rule S3: "Container artifacts state their posture, never inherit it: a rendered compose file, quadlet unit or manifest emits privileged off, every capability dropped, no-new-privileges, a non-root user, and bridge networking unless host is explicitly asked for ... Each emitted negative is pinned by a golden plus a test forbidding the widening tokens." Classification per item, all three platforms: privileged off -- inherited from the engine default; capabilities dropped -- absent (docker/podman keep their default set, kubernetes keeps the runtime default); no-new-privileges / allowPrivilegeEscalation:false -- absent; seccomp -- inherited; non-root identity -- absent, and worse, the artifacts silently assume uid 0: a kubernetes secret volume at defaultMode 0400 without fsGroup and a podman application.yml written 0600 are readable only by root inside the container (the guide itself calls the 0400 case a 'latent hazard' at userguide.md:1726-1730); read-only root -- absent and not documented as unsupported; host networking -- bridge, with ports as the operator's list (correct, emitted). Nothing in deploy_test.go, dockergen_test.go, podmangen_test.go or gen/golden_test.go asserts the absence of a widening token, so the next edit that adds `cap_add` or `privileged: true` passes every gate. The patch states the uncontroversial negatives on all three platforms (a JVM needs no capability and never escalates); runAsNonRoot/User= and readOnlyRootFilesystem need the image's uid and writable paths first (see gaps) and belong in a follow-up with the goldens. Every full-document golden (deploy_test.go:81-209, dockergen_test.go:59-117/149-174, podmangen_test.go:73-135, gen/golden_test.go:346-451, and any in main_test.go) must gain the same lines, plus one negative test per renderer over the widening tokens.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/deploy/deploy.go
+++ b/internal/deploy/deploy.go
@@ -372,6 +372,15 @@ func renderDeployment(w *yw, in Input, inst Instance, ns, credRef, storeRef string, hasStores bo
 	w.Line(6, "containers:")
 	w.Line(8, "- name: "+spec.ConnectorContainerName)
 	w.Line(10, "image: "+inst.Image)
+	// Stated rather than inherited: a JVM needs no capability and never
+	// escalates, so the negatives are spelled out where a reviewer reads them.
+	w.Line(10, "securityContext:")
+	w.Line(12, "allowPrivilegeEscalation: false")
+	w.Line(12, "capabilities:")
+	w.Line(14, "drop:")
+	w.Line(16, "- ALL")
+	w.Line(12, "seccompProfile:")
+	w.Line(14, "type: RuntimeDefault")
 	w.Line(10, "ports:")
 	w.Line(12, "- name: management")
 	w.Line(14, "containerPort: "+strconv.Itoa(mgmtPort))
--- a/internal/dockergen/dockergen.go
+++ b/internal/dockergen/dockergen.go
@@ -112,6 +112,13 @@ func renderService(w *yw, in Input, inst Instance) {
 	w.Line(2, inst.Name+":")
 	w.Line(4, "image: "+inst.Image)
 	w.Line(4, "container_name: "+inst.Name)
+	// Runtime posture, stated rather than inherited: neither docker nor podman
+	// drops anything unless told to.
+	w.Line(4, "privileged: false")
+	w.Line(4, "cap_drop:")
+	w.Line(6, "- ALL")
+	w.Line(4, "security_opt:")
+	w.Line(6, "- no-new-privileges=true")
 	// labels: le-mode is always set; role: active only for standalone and
 	// active_active -- an active_standby role is only knowable live from the
 	// actuator, so it is never asserted statically here.
--- a/internal/podmangen/podmangen.go
+++ b/internal/podmangen/podmangen.go
@@ -138,6 +138,10 @@ func RenderQuadlet(in Input) Unit {
 	w.Line(0, "[Container]")
 	w.Line(0, "Image="+inst.Image)
 	w.Line(0, "ContainerName="+inst.Name)
+	// Runtime posture, stated rather than inherited. NoNewPrivileges= belongs
+	// in [Container]: in [Service] it would bind podman itself.
+	w.Line(0, "DropCapability=all")
+	w.Line(0, "NoNewPrivileges=true")
 	for _, l := range leaderLabels(inst.LeaderMode) {
 		w.Line(0, "Label="+l[0]+"="+l[1])

Options are a freshness marker the `graphify` task writes and a cheap test compares against `git ls-files` hashes, or keeping only the small artifacts (GRAPH_REPORT.md, graph.json) tracked and regenerating graph.html locally. No patch: the choice belongs to the owner.

Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    git describe --tags --dirty: v0.10.1-dirty
    git log --oneline -- graphify-out/cache/last_query_stamp | wc -l: 24
    scripts/dev.sh
    65  # --dirty can never fire there -- only a local build off an unclean tree
    66  # ever reports a "-dirty" suffix.
    67  VERSION="$(git describe --tags --dirty 2>/dev/null)" || VERSION="dev"
    73      go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=$VERSION" -o "$DIST/$BIN_NAME" ./cmd/solmq-conn-util
    .gitignore
    18  # graphify per-machine state: the interpreter path is one host's absolute path, so

    20  graphify-out/.graphify_python
    /usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/graphify/cli.py

    692          stamp = Path(graph_path).parent / "cache" / "last_query_stamp"
    ... (3 more lines in the finding record)

Why it matters: graphify writes a wall-clock timestamp into graphify-out/cache/last_query_stamp on every query/explain/path (cli.py:687-694) so its hook-guard can judge freshness (cli.py:699-707). Because the file is tracked, the working tree is dirty after any query -- observed at HEAD with nothing else modified -- and `git describe --tags --dirty` returns v0.10.1-dirty, which dev.sh:67/dev.ps1:79 bake into -X main.version (dev.sh:73, dev.ps1:86). A local `dev.sh build` after reading the graph therefore reports a dirty binary with no source change, and a developer who learns to ignore '-dirty' loses the signal for real uncommitted edits. The project CLAUDE.md (6) mandates a query before codebase questions, so every session hits this, and 24 commits have already churned the stamp. The sibling per-machine file .graphify_python is ignored for exactly this reason (.gitignore:18-20). Release builds are unaffected (clean tag checkout), hence minor. The patch adds the ignore line; the file must also be untracked, user-run: git rm --cached graphify-out/cache/last_query_stamp. Tracking the rest of graphify-out/ is a documented choice (.gitignore:16 'live graph stays tracked').

 graphify-out/.graphify_python

#### CR-0123 [minor] [new] Container identity is inherited from the image on every platform, and the 0400 credentials volume depends on that unstated identity

Location: internal/deploy/deploy.go:345-349, internal/deploy/deploy.go:479-484, internal/dockergen/dockergen.go:166-172, internal/podmangen/podmangen.go:162-168, docs/userguide.md:1723-1730
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    Posture grep 7 (`runAsUser|runAsGroup|fsGroup|^ *user:|^User=|^Group=|securityContext|runAsNonRoot`) over the three renderer packages and testdata/golden: hits only on `user:` MQ credential fields in application.yml/specs, none in a rendered artifact.
    internal/deploy/deploy.go:
    345 	w.Line(4, "spec:")
    349 	w.Line(6, "automountServiceAccountToken: false")
    480 		w.Line(8, "- name: secrets")
    481 		w.Line(10, "secret:")
    482 		w.Line(12, "secretName: "+credRef)
    483 		w.Line(12, "defaultMode: 0400")
    internal/dockergen/dockergen.go:169-170 `- source: n` / `target: SecretsMountPath/n` (no mode/uid/gid)
    internal/podmangen/podmangen.go:167 `Secret=<store>,type=mount,target=...` (no mode=/uid=)
    docs/userguide.md:1726-1730: "defaultMode: 0400 is a separate, latent hazard ... with no fsGroup set, 0400 files are unreadable by the container's running user".

Why it matters: House rule S3 asks for a non-root identity emitted explicitly (runAsUser/runAsGroup/fsGroup, compose user:, quadlet User=/Group=), not inherited from the image. None of the three artifacts states who the connector runs as, so a change of USER in the image silently changes the deployment's posture. The kubernetes Secret volume at 0400 (483) is owned by root unless fsGroup is set, so the credentials are readable only if the image happens to run as root -- the user guide documents this as a latent hazard (1726-1730) but the manifest neither sets fsGroup nor runAsNonRoot, so the two settings are not kept consistent by the tool; any future identity emission must set fsGroup (or raise defaultMode to 0440) in the same change or every ${...} placeholder stays unresolved. On compose and quadlet the secret files take the engine default (0444, root-owned) because mode/uid/gid are not emitted. Classification: identity inherited from the image on all three platforms; secret owner/mode inherited from engine defaults. Suggested shape: a pod-level securityContext with runAsNonRoot: true and fsGroup, `user:` in compose and `User=`/`Group=` in the quadlet, taken from a single documented spec value, with the connector image's documented uid as the default.

Change: as described above

Why it matters: 1. kubernetes.deployment.replica: 3 (typo) decodes to Replicas 0, applyKubeDefaults sets 1, validate passes, one pod runs. kubernetes.service.enable: true renders no Service. docker.project_name: x yields the default project. podman.basedir: is the only such typo that is caught, and only because base-dir happens to be required. 2. The project knows this and compensates per key: every removed key keeps a struct field whose sole purpose is to be rejected by validate (Deployment.Image/Timezone, Kubernetes.Logging, Docker.Image/Timezone/Secrets/Stores, Podman.Mode/Quadlet/Image/Timezone/Secrets/Stores, LibsMount.MountPath, CredCreate.Source/Variables/ValuesFile, Security.Enabled, Management.Exposure, rawLeader.Solace), plus a custom UnmarshalYAML for java-options and a second generic-tree decode for transform keys. That is a duplicated concept (strictness re-implemented key by key) and a change-safety cost: every future removal must add a sentinel and a validate branch, and every future live key is unprotected until someone mistypes it. 3. Interfaces checklist: every config key validated at load with an error naming the key. The guide states the same standard for ${VAR} at userguide.md:526 ("A typo must not vanish silently"); the test comment says non-strict parsing is not endorsed. 4. Fix: yaml.NewDecoder(...).KnownFields(true) in ParseEnv (treat io.EOF as an empty document, as the doc comment promises). The sentinel fields stay declared, so validate's tailored messages still fire. Note the inner node.Decode calls in CredentialsSecret/StoresSecret.UnmarshalYAML (kubernetes.go:92-110, 132-150) are non-strict for their own sub-keys and need the same treatment; TestParseEnvUnknownKeyIgnored inverts; ParseWorkflow (out of this lane) deserves the same review.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/spec/env.go
+++ b/internal/spec/env.go
@@ -1,7 +1,10 @@
 package spec
 
 import (
+	"bytes"
+	"errors"
 	"fmt"
+	"io"
 
 	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
 )
@@ -50,7 +53,12 @@ type rawWorkflows struct {
 // ParseEnv decodes env.yaml into an Env, applying every section's defaults. An
 // empty/absent file yields a zero Env with default discovery (dir ".", "*").
 func ParseEnv(data []byte) (*Env, error) {
 	var raw rawEnv
-	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, &raw); err != nil {
+	// Strict: a key no struct declares is an error naming it, so a typo in a
+	// live key cannot vanish into a default. The retired fields stay declared,
+	// so validate still reports them with their tailored messages.
+	dec := yaml.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
+	dec.KnownFields(true)
+	if err := dec.Decode(&raw); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("env.yaml: %v", err)
 	}
```

#### CR-0130 [minor] [new] Teardown in GenerateKubernetes still resolves every credential and store, piping plaintext to kubectl delete

Location: internal/gen/gen.go:185-199, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:537-546, internal/deploy/deploy.go:169-197, internal/runner/runner.go:402-403
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go
      537	manifest, errs, warns := gen.GenerateKubernetes(req, resolver(envDir),
      538		gen.KubeOpts{Teardown: action == runner.ActionRemove}, extraAllowed...)
    internal/gen/gen.go
      186	if c := k.Secrets.Credentials; c != nil && c.Create != nil {
      187		kvs, err := ResolveCredentials(b.model.Secrets, res)
      193	if s := k.Secrets.Stores; s != nil && s.Create != nil {
      194		files, err := resolveStores(&e.Defaults, res)
      472			return nil, fmt.Errorf("secret %s: environment variable %s is not set; export it before deploying", r.Stable, r.EnvVar)
    internal/deploy/deploy.go
      178		w.Line(0, "stringData:")
      179		for _, kv := range in.CredKVs {
      180			w.Line(2, kv.Key+": "+strconv.Quote(kv.Val))
    internal/runner/runner.go
      402	argv = append(argv, verb, "-f", "-")
    ... (2 more lines in the finding record)

Why it matters: A teardown is `kubectl delete -f -`, which matches objects by kind and name; the value of a Secret is irrelevant. Yet GenerateKubernetes resolves every -env credential from the environment, reads both .jks files and builds the registry pull payload under Teardown too, so (1) `remove` fails with "export it before deploying" when a credential variable is not exported or a truststore file has since moved -- the one situation (decommissioning, a different operator's shell) where the secrets are least likely to be at hand -- and (2) every credential value and store byte travels on kubectl's stdin for no purpose (and into kubectl's own output under -v). The podman teardown already works from names only. The patch below skips the credentials and stores resolution under Teardown; the Secret documents are still emitted (empty stringData/data) so they are deleted. The image-pull Secret still needs a small deploy.Render change to emit a name-only Secret when DockerConfigJSON is empty under Teardown; the remove golden in the gen tests will change accordingly.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/gen/gen.go
+++ b/internal/gen/gen.go
@@ -183,14 +183,18 @@ func GenerateKubernetes(r Request, res Resolver, opts KubeOpts, extraAllowed ...string) (out string, errs, warns []Issue) {
 	}
 
 	in := deploy.Input{Kube: k, Defaults: &e.Defaults, Syslog: e.Defaults.Syslog, Teardown: opts.Teardown}
-	if c := k.Secrets.Credentials; c != nil && c.Create != nil {
+	// A teardown is `delete -f -`, which matches objects by kind and name: no
+	// value is needed, so none is resolved. remove then neither demands every
+	// credential be exported nor pipes plaintext values to a delete. The Secret
+	// documents are still rendered (with empty data) so they are deleted.
+	if c := k.Secrets.Credentials; c != nil && c.Create != nil && !opts.Teardown {
 		kvs, err := ResolveCredentials(b.model.Secrets, res)
 		if err != nil {
 			return "", []Issue{{File: fileEnv, Msg: err.Error()}}, warns
 		}
 		in.CredKVs = kvs
 	}
-	if s := k.Secrets.Stores; s != nil && s.Create != nil {
+	if s := k.Secrets.Stores; s != nil && s.Create != nil && !opts.Teardown {
 		files, err := resolveStores(&e.Defaults, res)
 		if err != nil {
 			return "", []Issue{{File: fileEnv, Msg: err.Error()}}, warns
 		}
```

Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    parse.go
    733 			c.CPU.Used = s.cpu
    739 			// "512MiB / 15.6GiB" already carries both sides; keep it whole rather
    740 			// than splitting and re-joining it into a different spelling.
    741 			c.Memory.Used = s.mem
    742 			c.Memory.Limit = ""
    743 			c.Memory.Percent = s.memPct
    613 		c.CPU = &Resource{Limit: lim + " cpu"}

    180 // reports for it. Every field is a rendered string, not a number: each engine
    181 // reports in its own units

Why it matters: The model comment allows per-engine units, but ApplyStats goes further: on docker/podman memory.used holds both sides ('512MiB / 15.6GiB') and the limit ParseInspect recorded from HostConfig.Memory is thrown away (742), while cpu.used is a host-relative percentage ('0.50%') set against a limit in cores ('2 cpu'), rendering as '0.50% of 2 cpu'. On kubernetes used is a bare quantity and limit a bare quantity. A --output json consumer reading memory.used as a quantity works on one platform and breaks on the other, and SchemaVersion (a 'compatibility contract') does not say the field is platform-shaped. The in-code comment shows this was a deliberate table choice; the cost lands in the contract. Splitting the stats string on ' / ' into Used/Limit (and keeping the inspect limit when stats has none) makes the field uniform and the table reads '512MiB of 15.6GiB (3.28%)' like kubernetes.

#### CR-0191 [minor] [new] solmq-status Basic-auth header rides wget argv in get(), readable from the container's process list

Location: internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:215-221, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:1-7, docs/userguide.md:1017-1019
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    statusscript.go
    216   if [ -n "$PASS" ]; then
    217     wget -qO- --header="Authorization: Basic $(printf %s:%s "$USER_NAME" "$PASS" | base64 | tr -d ...)" "$1" 2>/dev/null
    4 // produces targets the connector image's busybox userland (Alpine's sh, sed,
    5 // wget, tr, base64, head, cat, sort, cut -- no curl, no jq, no bash)

Why it matters: The Authorization header, i.e. base64(user:password), is a wget argument, so for the duration of each request it is readable in /proc/<pid>/cmdline by anything in the container (and by the host), seven times per report and once per healthcheck tick (every 30 s on compose/podman, every 10 s on kubernetes) for the life of the container. The house rule is that secrets arrive as files and never on argv. Mitigating facts: it is the reserved read-only account whose password is a literal in application.yml by design (README), the viewer is already inside the same trust domain, and busybox wget offers no header-from-file or netrc path, so within the stated toolset there is no argv-free spelling. Reported so the trade-off is stated in the script header and docs/userguide.md 7.1 as an accepted limitation rather than left implicit; if the image ever gains curl, '-K -' (config on stdin) or '--netrc-file' would close it.

Change: as described above

#### CR-0208 [minor] [new] kubernetes.service.port is range-checked then silently dropped when service.enabled is unset in checkKube

Location: internal/validate/validate.go:707-711, internal/spec/kubernetes.go:34-37, internal/spec/kubernetes.go:387-389, internal/deploy/deploy.go:259-264, docs/userguide.md:1343-1343, docs/userguide.md:1343
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    kubernetes.go:34-37  type Service struct { Enabled bool `yaml:"enabled"`; Port Port `yaml:"port"` }
    kubernetes.go:387-389  if k.Service.Port == (Port{}) { k.Service.Port = Port{Host: mgmtPort, Container: mgmtPort} }
    validate.go:709-711  // ... range-check both sides regardless of service.enabled, since an unset port is already
                         // defaulted to management.port by the time validate sees it.
                         checkPortRange(add, "kubernetes.service.port", ctx.Kube.Service.Port)
    deploy.go:261-263  if in.Kube.Service.Enabled { sep(); renderService(w, in.Instance.Name, ns, in.Kube.Service.Port) }
    userguide.md:1343  | `service` | `enabled`, `port` | emit a Service on this port; `port` accepts a bare port or `host:container` ...; unset defaults to the effective management port |

Why it matters: An operator writes `service: { port: "8080:8090" }` (the shape the guide advertises) and omits enabled. applyKubeDefaults keeps the port, validate range-checks it (and would reject a bad one), generate succeeds -- and no Service is emitted because deploy gates on Enabled alone. Nothing says the port was dropped: a value is validated and then discarded, which is the implicit-downgrade pattern the design checklist flags (explicit over implicit; S4a fail loud vs skip). The 8.1 table never states that enabled defaults to false. A warning when enabled is false and the port differs from the mgmt:mgmt default closes it without changing output.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/validate/validate.go
+++ b/internal/validate/validate.go
@@ -711 +711,7 @@ func checkKube(add, warn func(string, string, ...any), ctx Context) {
 	checkPortRange(add, "kubernetes.service.port", ctx.Kube.Service.Port)
+	// A port written without enabled: true renders no Service at all (deploy
+	// emits one only when Service.Enabled), so say so instead of validating a
+	// value that is then dropped. The mgmt:mgmt default is indistinguishable
+	// from an explicit one, which is harmless: it changes nothing either way.
+	if mp := ctx.Defaults.EffectiveManagementPort(); !ctx.Kube.Service.Enabled && ctx.Kube.Service.Port != (spec.Port{Host: mp, Container: mp}) {
+		warn(fileEnv, "kubernetes.service.port is set but service.enabled is not true, so no Service is emitted; set service.enabled: true or remove service.port")
+	}

#### CR-0210 [minor] [new] empty, query-suffixed or duplicate libs.download url basenames pass checkLibs and break the initContainer

Location: internal/validate/validate.go:839-852, internal/deploy/deploy.go:358-367, internal/spec/targets.go:98-104, internal/deploy/deploy.go:360-363
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    deploy.go:360-363
      cmds := make([]string, 0, len(d.URLs))
      for _, u := range d.URLs {
      	cmds = append(cmds, "wget -O '/libs/"+spec.BaseName(u)+"' '"+u+"'")
      }
    deploy.go:367  w.Line(10, `command: ["sh", "-c", `+strconv.Quote(strings.Join(cmds, " && "))+`]`)
    validate.go:844-848
      for _, u := range d.URLs {
      	if !safeLibsURL(u) {
      		add(fileEnv, "libs.download url %q must be http(s) and contain no spaces, quotes, or control characters", u)
      	}
      }
    targets.go:98-104  func BaseName(p string) string { ... if i := strings.LastIndexByte(p, '/'); i >= 0 { return p[i+1:] } ... }

Why it matters: safeLibsURL guards the shell quoting (quotes, whitespace, $ and backslash are rejected, so the single-quoted argument cannot be escaped) but nothing looks at what the URL names. https://repo1/ibmmq/ (trailing slash) yields `wget -O '/libs/' '...'`, which fails at pod start as an initContainer error far from env.yaml; https://a/x.jar?v=1 saves as `x.jar?v=1`, which no `*.jar` classpath pattern matches; two URLs ending in the same file name silently overwrite each other in /libs. All three are knowable at validate time from the string alone (input validation at the edge). The patch adds the two unambiguous checks (non-empty basename, no duplicates); requiring a `.jar` suffix is a judgement call for the owners since the loader's pattern is not in this repo.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/validate/validate.go
+++ b/internal/validate/validate.go
@@ -844,5 +844,17 @@ func checkLibs(add func(string, string, ...any), k *spec.Kubernetes) {
+		seen := map[string]string{}
 		for _, u := range d.URLs {
 			if !safeLibsURL(u) {
 				add(fileEnv, "libs.download url %q must be http(s) and contain no spaces, quotes, or control characters", u)
+				continue
+			}
+			// The initContainer saves each download as /libs/<basename>, so the
+			// URL has to end in a file name and two URLs may not share one.
+			base := spec.BaseName(u)
+			if base == "" {
+				add(fileEnv, "libs.download url %q has no file name: the initContainer saves each download as /libs/<basename>", u)
+			} else if prev, dup := seen[base]; dup {
+				add(fileEnv, "libs.download urls %q and %q both save as /libs/%s; one would overwrite the other", prev, u, base)
+			} else {
+				seen[base] = u
 			}
 		}
```

-		for _, raw := range in.URLs {

-				return Report{}, fmt.Errorf("parsing url %q: %w", raw, err)

#### CR-0167 [minor] [new] Preflight answers a kubectl auth can-i 'no' with the log-in hint, misdirecting a logged-in user lacking RBAC

    runner.go:474-480

    475 if runErr != nil {
    476     hint, ok := preflightHints[platform]
    ...
    480     return out, fmt.Errorf("preflight failed for %s: %w\n%s", platform, runErr, hint)

Why it matters: 1. `kubectl auth can-i` answers an RBAC denial by printing 'no' and exiting 1 -- the same exit status as an unreachable or unauthenticated cluster. 2. Preflight treats every non-nil error identically and appends the login hint, so a logged-in operator who merely lacks `create deployment` (or, after the read probe fix, `get pods`) is told to log in. 3. The output 'no' is printed by report() above the error, but the actionable line points the wrong way; the error rule asks for what failed and what to do next. The probe's own stdout already distinguishes the two cases.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/runner/runner.go
+++ b/internal/runner/runner.go
@@ -473,6 +473,12 @@ func Preflight(r Runner, platform, command, action, namespace string, extraAllowed []string) (string, error) {
 	out, runErr := r.Run(Cmd{Argv: argv})
 	if runErr != nil {
+		// `auth can-i` answers a denial with "no" and exit 1: the operator is
+		// logged in and lacks the permission, which the login hint misdescribes.
+		if platform == validate.PlatformKubernetes && strings.TrimSpace(out) == "no" {
+			return out, fmt.Errorf("preflight failed for %s: `%s` answered no; the current context lacks that permission -- ask for it or select another context, then re-run", platform, strings.Join(argv[1:], " "))

 		hint, ok := preflightHints[platform]
 		if !ok {
 			return out, fmt.Errorf("preflight failed for %s: %w", platform, runErr)

#### CR-0319 [nit] [new] syslogLine tells an operator with a renamed 2.x image that env.yaml names no release

Location: internal/libs/libs.go:193-203, internal/libs/image.go:210-224
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    libs.go:
    194:	tag, connector, ok := connectorRelease(deployedImage)
    195:	switch {
    196:	case !ok:
    197:		return 0, fmt.Sprintf("the newest release: env.yaml names no connector release to match it to -- a connector before %d.0 ships Jackson 2 and needs an %d.x encoder, so pin one with --version", ...)
    image.go:
    211:	name, tag, ok := imageNameTag(ref)
    212:	if !ok || name != embeddedListImage || !releaseTag(tag) {
    213:		return "", 0, false
    214:	}

Why it matters: connectorRelease folds three different situations into one false: no tag, a non-release tag such as latest, and an image whose last path element is not 'solace-pubsub-connector-ibmmq'. An operator who mirrors the image as `registry.corp/mirror/ibmmq-connector:2.14.1` -- a plain 2.x connector -- is told 'env.yaml names no connector release' although it names 2.14.1, and the syslog set defaults to the newest encoder (Jackson 3), which fails on that connector at start. builtinList (image.go:263-265) already distinguishes the renamed-image case with its own sentence; syslogLine should say the same thing ('env.yaml deploys <ref>, which is not the connector image the lines are known for') so the remedy (--version 8.x) is obvious. A follow-on design question, not raised as a finding: when the line is unknown, defaulting to the newest encoder picks the one line no built-in list yet describes.

#### CR-0037 [minor] [new] Agent-run `graphify update .` instruction in project CLAUDE.md contradicts the user-run graph-refresh rule

Location: CLAUDE.md:6-9, scripts/dev.sh:146-150, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:33-35, .claude/settings.json:5-10, .claude/settings.json:15-20, CLAUDE.md:9-9, /home/hafio/.claude/CLAUDE.md:1-1, CLAUDE.md:9
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    CLAUDE.md:9: - After modifying code, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current (AST-only, no API cost).
    CLAUDE.md:6: For codebase questions, first run `graphify query "<question>"` ... :8: Read graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md only for broad architecture review or when query/path/explain do not surface enough context.
    ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md S1: "If it verifies, builds, scans, or mutates state, you never run it ... That covers every dev-script task (build, vet/lint, test, cov, scan, image, up/down, graphify -- S7)"
    ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md S2: "Graph refreshes -- incremental or full -- are user-run like every gate (S1); when the graph is stale, propose the task." and "consult the knowledge graph before grepping: its report first, then a read-only query, then only the files it points to."
    scripts/dev.sh:146-150: task_graphify() { ... run graphify graphify update . }

Why it matters: Two instructions govern the same action and disagree: the project file orders an unattended `graphify update .` after every code change, while the global file makes graphify a user-run dev-script task (there is one, dev.sh:146-150) and says to propose it. They also disagree on lookup order (project: query first, report last; global: report first, then a read-only query). The global preamble lets a project file override it, but nothing in CLAUDE.md says this is a deliberate override -- it is the graphify skill's stock boilerplate -- so an agent following either file violates the other, and `graphify update` rewrites tracked files under graphify-out/ (dev.sh:146 comment: a developer artifact). Resolve by pointing the project rule at the dev-script task and the user.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/CLAUDE.md
+++ b/CLAUDE.md
@@ -8,2 +8,2 @@
 - Read graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md only for broad architecture review or when query/path/explain do not surface enough context.
-- After modifying code, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current (AST-only, no API cost).
+- After modifying code, propose `./scripts/dev.sh graphify` (= `graphify update .`, AST-only, no API cost); like every dev-script task it is user-run (global CLAUDE.md S1/S2), never run by the agent.
```

#### CR-0095 [minor] [new] The documented 0600 guarantee for files carrying the status password does not hold on Windows, where Go file modes only toggle the read-only attribute

Location: docs/userguide.md:1555-1558, docs/userguide.md:1015-1016, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:210-211, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:660, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:1393, internal/runner/runner.go:378-388, internal/runner/runner.go:375-377, docs/test.md:550-551
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    userguide.md:1556-1557 `\`application.yml\` is written file` / `mode \`0600\` (it carries the \`solmq-status\` account's literal password); the status` / 1558 `script, the logback config, and the unit itself are \`0644\`.`
    userguide.md:1015 `that last one is written with file mode \`0600\``
    DEVELOPMENT.md:210-211 `Credential` / `env-files are written \`0600\` and never logged.`
    main.go:1393 `if err := os.WriteFile(out, []byte(content), 0o600); err != nil {` (generate -o, whose application.yml/compose carry the status password)
    runner.go:376 `// needed. Secret material (credential env-files) is written with mode 0600 and`
    docs/test.md:550 `| TestWriteFileCreatesDirsAndMode | - | creates nested dirs, writes content, sets mode 0600 (non-windows) |`

Why it matters: Go's os package documents that on Windows only the 0o200 (owner-writable) bit of a mode is honoured; os.WriteFile(..., 0o600) and (..., 0o644) therefore produce identical files that inherit the parent directory's ACLs. The test catalogue already scopes the mode tests to non-Windows, but every user-facing statement (7.1, 8.3, DEVELOPMENT.md) is unconditional, and the README ships a windows-amd64 binary. On Windows the realistic exposure is `generate ... -o application.yml` / `-o docker-compose.yml` (main.go:1393) in a shared directory, since the podman path cannot complete there anyway (see the systemd finding). Documented as a platform note it is harmless; stated as a guarantee it is wrong.

Change: see the description above; a speculative diff was withheld

TestTestCatalogSnapshotInSync gates only counts (testcatalog_test.go:55-90), so neither row fails any gate. S6: 'renamed or removed symbols leave no stale references'.

#### CR-0222 [minor] [new] task_scan fatal on unfixable govulncheck findings; DEVELOPMENT.md's 'all fixable' premise is false

Location: scripts/dev.sh:119-130, scripts/dev.ps1:134-145, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:44-45
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    scripts/dev.sh
    119  # One task, every applicable check. FATAL on fixable CVEs. solmq-conn-util ships no
    120  # image, so this is the Go dependency scan alone. govulncheck reports only vulns
    121  # reachable from called code -- all actionable -- so a non-zero exit stops the
    129    run scan go tool govulncheck ./...
    docs/DEVELOPMENT.md
    44  `scan` is `go tool govulncheck ./...`, fatal on any finding -- every Go vuln-DB finding is
    45  reachable-and-fixable, so there is nothing to warn-and-pass on.
    ~/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/x/vuln@v1.6.0/internal/scan/text.go
    81    if (isCalled(h.findings) && h.scanLevel == govulncheck.ScanLevelSymbol) ||
    84      return errVulnerabilitiesFound
    305    h.style(keyStyle, "Fixed in: ")
    306    if fixedVersion != "" {
    307      h.print(path, "@", fixedVersion)
    308    } else {
    ... (3 more lines in the finding record)

Why it matters: govulncheck exits 3 whenever any called-level finding exists (text.go:81-84, errors.go:17) and it explicitly renders findings that have no fixed version as 'Fixed in: N/A' (text.go:305-310) -- so unfixable entries do occur in the Go vuln DB and the tool does not distinguish them by exit code. dev.sh:129/dev.ps1:144 treat every non-zero exit as fatal and the dispatch loop stops (dev.sh:190-196), which makes `all scan` (ci.yml:60) and the tag pipeline's gates (tag.yml:88-93) red with no override ('There is no report-only mode'). That is the opposite of what the contract asks for on unfixable CVEs. The deviation is documented (DEVELOPMENT.md:44-45, dev.sh:120-121), which makes it a deliberate choice, but its stated premise is false: the day a reachable stdlib or yaml.v3 vulnerability lands without a fix, releases freeze until upstream ships one. Likelihood is low for a one-dependency module, hence minor. Implementing the contract means `govulncheck -json` plus a filter on `fixed_version` (govulncheck.go:150); the alternative is to reword the docs to say the freeze is accepted rather than impossible.

Change: as described above

#### CR-0223 [minor] [new] Previous cov total destroyed by log_begin / Start-TaskLog truncation before task_cov appends the new one

Location: scripts/dev.sh:28-30, scripts/dev.ps1:33-37, scripts/dev.sh:107-117, scripts/dev.ps1:120-132, scripts/dev.sh:187-187, scripts/dev.ps1:196-196, scripts/dev.sh:27-30, scripts/dev.sh:107-116, scripts/dev.ps1:120-131, scripts/dev.sh:187
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    dev.sh:27  # Truncate this task's log with a header, then everything tees onto it.
    dev.sh:28  log_begin() {
    dev.sh:29    printf '=== %s | %s ===\n' "$(now)" "$1" > "$LOG_DIR/$1.log"
    dev.sh:109   # The previous total in logs/cov.log is the floor (local only -- CI is a
    dev.sh:110   # fresh checkout with no prior log).
    dev.sh:116   go tool cover -func=coverage.out | tail -n1 | tee -a "$LOG_DIR/cov.log"
    dev.sh:187   log_begin "$task"            (runs before "task_$task" at 190)
    dev.ps1:35   Set-Content -Path (Get-Log $Task) -Encoding utf8 `
    dev.ps1:36     -Value ("=== {0} | {1} ===" -f (Get-Now), $Task)
    scripts/logs/cov.log (local, 2026-10-01): exactly one 'total:' line (96.6%) then the footer
    Global CLAUDE.md S5: "The coverage floor is the last recorded total. `cov` prints and logs it, so the previous total in the cov log is the bar. ... An unexplained drop is a failed gate"

Why it matters: The house rule makes the previous cov total the gate, and dev.sh:109-110 says the previous total 'in logs/cov.log is the floor'. But the dispatcher calls log_begin (dev.sh:187 / dev.ps1:196) before the task runs, and log_begin truncates the file with `>` (Set-Content in PowerShell), so by the time the new total is appended at dev.sh:116 / dev.ps1:129 the old total no longer exists anywhere. The log therefore always holds exactly one total (confirmed in the local scripts/logs/cov.log), the comparison the rule relies on can only be made by a human who read the old file before running, and a drop is invisible to anyone who did not -- which is the normal case after `full`. The log header truncation is contract behaviour; the fix is to carry the one line that matters across it so the floor and the new total sit side by side in the same log.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/scripts/dev.sh
+++ b/scripts/dev.sh
@@ -26,7 +26,14 @@
 
 # Truncate this task's log with a header, then everything tees onto it.
+# cov keeps one line from the old log: its total is the floor the new run is
+# measured against, and truncating it first would destroy the baseline.
 log_begin() {
+  local prev=""
+  if [ "$1" = cov ]; then
+    prev=$(grep -E '^total:' "$LOG_DIR/cov.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -n1)
+  fi
   printf '=== %s | %s ===\n' "$(now)" "$1" > "$LOG_DIR/$1.log"
+  if [ -n "$prev" ]; then printf 'floor (previous run): %s\n' "$prev" >> "$LOG_DIR/$1.log"; fi
 }
--- a/scripts/dev.ps1
+++ b/scripts/dev.ps1
@@ -32,8 +32,15 @@
 
 function Start-TaskLog {
   param($Task)
+  # cov keeps one line from the old log: its total is the floor (see dev.sh).
+  $prev = $null
+  if ($Task -eq 'cov' -and (Test-Path (Get-Log $Task))) {
+    $prev = Get-Content (Get-Log $Task) | Where-Object { $_ -like 'total:*' } | Select-Object -Last 1
+  }
   Set-Content -Path (Get-Log $Task) -Encoding utf8 `
     -Value ("=== {0} | {1} ===" -f (Get-Now), $Task)
+  if ($prev) { Add-Content -Path (Get-Log $Task) -Value "floor (previous run): $prev" -Encoding utf8 }
 }
```

    main.go: `var promptLine = readStdinLine`, `var stdinIsTerminal = func() bool {...}`, `var stderrIsTerminal = func() bool {...}` -- each commented "A var rather than a func ... so a hard-coded probe would make every path behind it unreachable from a test." progress.go:61-67: "progressFrameRate and progressNow are the two test seams, vars for the same reason stdinIsTerminal is one" / `var ( progressFrameRate = 120 * time.Millisecond; progressNow = time.Now )`. main_test.go:4292-4300 withStderrTerminal/withProgressClock reassign them with t.Cleanup. House rule S4a: "No global state. Pass an explicit application context; never reach for globals."

Why it matters: Documented and deliberate, but it is exactly the pattern the rule names: production code reads process-wide mutable state, and every test that touches one of the five seams must run serially (none can call t.Parallel without racing another test's swap), which already makes the 6300-line main_test.go a single serial suite. The runner.Runner seam shows the house style the project otherwise follows -- an injected value threaded through dispatch. A small `term` struct (prompt, stdinIsTerminal, stderrIsTerminal, now) carried in statusOpts/instanceRequest would make the seams explicit and the tests parallelisable. No patch: a cross-cutting refactor to be scoped on its own.

#### CR-0336 [nit] [new] AllowedCommands is a package-level mutable map rather than a read-only accessor

Location: internal/validate/validate.go:37-46, internal/validate/validate.go:1203
Confidence: verified
Evidence:

    validate.go:42-46
      var AllowedCommands = map[string][]string{
      	PlatformKubernetes: {"kubectl", "oc"},
      	PlatformDocker:     {"docker"},
      	PlatformPodman:     {"podman"},
      }
    validate.go:1203  allowed := AllowedCommands[platform]
    validate_deploycommand_test.go:69  strings.Join(AllowedCommands[PlatformKubernetes], ", ")   (the only external reader)

Why it matters: House rule S4a: "No global state. Pass an explicit application context; never reach for globals." The allowlist is the security boundary for argv[0] and is exported as a writable map: any importer (or a test running in the same process) can `validate.AllowedCommands["docker"] = append(..., "sh")` and every later CheckDeployCommand honours it, with no trace in the Context that carries the per-invocation --allow-command extension. Go cannot make a map const, but an unexported table behind `func AllowedCommands(platform string) []string` returning a copy keeps the allowlist read-only by construction; the one test reader adapts trivially. Nit because nothing in the repo mutates it today.

#### CR-0344 [major] [new] get() loses the health document on a 503, so a DOWN instance reports no health lines and the healthcheck logs 'unreachable'

Location: docs/userguide.md:2372, internal/render/render.go:311, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:215-221, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:341-359, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:289-299, docs/userguide.md:2384-2386
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    statusscript.go
    215 get() {
    216   if [ -n "$PASS" ]; then
    217     wget -qO- --header="Authorization: Basic ..." "$1" 2>/dev/null
    218   else
    219     wget -qO- "$1" 2>/dev/null
    291   H=$(get "$BASE/health" | health_status)
    295   echo "${H:-unreachable}"
    341 HEALTH=$(get "$BASE/health") || HEALTH=""
    342 if [ -n "$HEALTH" ]; then
    347     # Not-UP is the case the detail is for, and show-details is always on, so
    350     echo "health: ${H:-unknown}"
    351     echo "health-detail: $HEALTH"
    359 fi
    userguide.md 2384: 'UP, or the status plus a health-detail line carrying the whole document (show-details is always on, so it names the failing component)'

Why it matters: Spring Boot's health endpoint maps DOWN and OUT_OF_SERVICE to HTTP 503 by default (management.endpoint.health.status.http-mapping). busybox wget -- the only HTTP client the package comment allows for -- treats any non-2xx/3xx status as fatal: it prints 'server returned error: HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable' to stderr (discarded by 2>/dev/null), writes nothing to stdout and exits non-zero; it has no --content-on-error. So exactly when the connector is not UP: (1) in the report, $HEALTH is empty, the whole block at 342-359 prints nothing -- no health:, no health-detail:, no health components: -- even though the comment at 346-351 and the user guide promise the detail precisely then; the operator sees leader-election and workflow lines and reads the missing health line as 'endpoint answered nothing'; (2) in --health mode H is empty, so the engine's health log records 'unreachable' for a connector that actually answered DOWN (the exit code 1 is still right, so the verdict stands but the recorded cause is wrong and indistinguishable from a wrong port or a 401). The tests feed documents straight into health_status/health_components and never exercise get(), so the suite cannot see this. Confirm inside the image: 'wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:<port>/actuator/health; echo $?' against a DOWN instance (expect empty output, exit 1). Fixes: capture wget's stderr status line (-S, or the 'server returned error: HTTP/1.1 NNN' text) and report 'health: DOWN (HTTP 503)' when no body arrives; or render management.endpoint.health.status.http-mapping down/out-of-service = 200 into application.yml so the body always arrives (the readiness/healthcheck verdict keys off the status string, not the HTTP code, so it is not weakened), noting the effect on external HTTP monitors. In either case the --health branch should print the cause it saw rather than a blanket 'unreachable'.

Location: internal/podmangen/podmangen.go:169-182, internal/dockergen/dockergen.go:190-198, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:655-670
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    internal/podmangen/podmangen.go:169-182
      169: w.Line(0, "Volume="+inst.AppYAMLPath+":"+appYAMLTarget+":ro")
      171: w.Line(0, "Volume="+m.Source+":"+m.Target+":ro")
      174: w.Line(0, "Volume="+in.Libs.Source+":"+in.Libs.Target+":ro")
      179: w.Line(0, "Volume="+inst.StatusScriptPath+":"+statusTarget+":ro")
      182: w.Line(0, "Volume="+inst.LogbackPath+":"+logback.ContainerPath+":ro")
    internal/dockergen/dockergen.go:193  w.Line(6, "- "+s.Source+":"+s.Target+":ro")
    internal/dockergen/dockergen.go:196  w.Line(6, "- "+in.Libs.Source+":"+in.Libs.Target+":ro")
    cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:660-670 WriteFile into plan.BaseDir (e.g. /opt/solmq-connector) with no relabel.
    internal/spec/targets.go:81-89 the project targets RHEL/OpenShift explicitly (CRI-O /run/secrets note); grep -i selinux over docs/ and README.md: no hit.

Why it matters: podman on RHEL/Fedora runs containers under SELinux (container_t). A file written under /opt/<base-dir> by the operator gets the directory's default type (usr_t or default_t), which container_t may not read; without `:z`/`:Z` on the mount, the container sees EACCES on application.yml, the status script and the jar directory. Spring then starts with no config (the configtree import is optional and the external location is simply unreadable), the healthcheck's `sh /app/external/.status-script` fails, and `status` reports unhealthy with nothing pointing at SELinux. The same applies to the compose volumes when `docker.command` is podman (the Docker struct comment suggests it) or when dockerd runs with --selinux-enabled. Options: emit `:ro,Z` on the base-dir files (private label; they belong to this instance alone) and `:ro,z` on tls files and libs.dir (shared with other consumers), or document `chcon -Rt container_file_t <base-dir>` as a prerequisite. Confirm on an enforcing host with `ausearch -m avc -ts recent` after a deploy, or `getenforce` plus the unit's journal.

Change: as described above

To confirm: On an enforcing RHEL/Fedora host with container-selinux installed: `sesearch -A -s container_t -t usr_t -c file -p read` (and the same for -t user_home_t and -t default_t) to see which host labels container_t may read without a relabel; or run a `deploy podman` against the default /opt/solmq-connector base-dir and check `ausearch -m avc -ts recent` plus `podman run --rm -v /opt/solmq-connector/application.yml:/f:ro <image> cat /f`. A denial on usr_t confirms the headline; a denial only on user_home_t/default_t confirms the libs/tls-store variant. | On an enforcing RHEL host (getenforce), run deploy with rootless podman and a base-dir under $HOME, then 'ausearch -m avc -ts recent' for container_t denials on application.yml / the status script; separately 'sesearch -A -s container_t -t usr_t -c file -p read' decides whether an /opt base-dir is affected too. For compose, docker-ce is unaffected unless dockerd runs --selinux-enabled or docker.command is podman. | On an SELinux-enforcing RHEL host (`getenforce` == Enforcing), run `deploy` for the podman target with the documented base-dir and with a home-relative base-dir, then `ls -Z <base-dir>` and `ausearch -m avc -ts recent` (or `journalctl -u <unit>`) after the unit starts: an AVC denial on application.yml or the status script with scontext container_t confirms the finding; a clean start against usr_t-labelled /opt narrows it to non-/opt base-dirs and the tls/libs mounts.


#### CR-0346 [major] [new] downloaded jars land at CreateTemp's 0600 mode in writeAtomic

Location: internal/podmangen/podmangen.go:174, internal/libs/libs.go:834-875, internal/dockergen/dockergen.go:196, internal/libs/libs.go:834-838, internal/libs/libs.go:869-875, internal/libs/libs.go:833-838, internal/libs/libs.go:869-876, internal/podmangen/podmangen.go:451
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    internal/libs/libs.go
      833	dir := filepath.Dir(dst)
      834	tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, ".libs-download-*.tmp")
      869	if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
      872	if err := os.Rename(tmpPath, dst); err != nil {
      875	done = true
      (os.CreateTemp opens O_RDWR|O_CREATE|O_EXCL with perm 0600; nothing chmods the file before the rename)
    internal/dockergen/dockergen.go
      196			w.Line(6, "- "+in.Libs.Source+":"+in.Libs.Target+":ro")
    internal/podmangen/podmangen.go
      451		w.Line(0, "Volume="+in.Libs.Source+":"+in.Libs.Target+":ro")

Why it matters: writeAtomic's temp file is created by os.CreateTemp, which always uses mode 0600, and the rename keeps that mode, so every jar `download jar` produces is owner-only. The whole point of the directory is to be bind-mounted read-only into the connector (docker/podman libs.dir) or copied onto the libs PVC; a container whose process uid differs from the host user who ran download (rootful docker with a non-root image user, an NFS export without root squash mapping, a shared libs dir prepared by one operator and mounted by another) sees the files but cannot open them, and the JVM reports the MQ client classes as missing at startup rather than a permission problem. A jar is public artifact content, not a secret; the mode is an accident of the atomic-write helper. The runtime effect depends on the uid mapping (not verified here); the mode itself is certain. Patch: set 0644 before the rename so the jar lands with the mode `wget -O` would have given it.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/libs/libs.go
+++ b/internal/libs/libs.go
@@ -869,6 +869,13 @@ func writeAtomic(resp *http.Response, dst string, expectedSHA1 string) error {
 	if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
 		return fmt.Errorf("closing temp file: %w", err)
 	}
+	// CreateTemp made the file 0600. A jar is not a secret, and the libs dir is
+	// bind-mounted (or copied to a PVC) for a container running as some other
+	// uid, which cannot read an owner-only file: give it the mode a plain
+	// `wget -O` would, so the classpath is readable where it is mounted.
+	if err := os.Chmod(tmpPath, 0o644); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("setting permissions on %s: %w", filepath.Base(dst), err)
+	}
 	if err := os.Rename(tmpPath, dst); err != nil {
 		return fmt.Errorf("renaming into place: %w", err)
 	}
```

To confirm: The default USER of solace/solace-pubsub-connector-ibmmq (docker image inspect --format '{{.Config.User}}'); if it is non-root, a rootless podman deploy with libs.dir populated by 'download jar' fails to read the jars (EACCES / NoClassDefFoundError) with no change to the download report. | Inspect the connector image's configured user (e.g. `docker image inspect <image> --format '{{.Config.User}}'`) and, on a host where `download jar mq` was run, `ls -l libs/` (expect -rw-------) followed by a docker compose or rootless podman start of the rendered unit: a non-root image user should produce ClassNotFound/NoClassDefFoundError for com.ibm.mq classes or an EACCES on the mounted jars.

#### CR-0347 [major] [new] ApplyTop misreads kubectl top's five-field --all-namespaces rows, so --all --details silently shows no usage

Location: internal/statusreport/parse.go:454-478, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:481-491, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:244-247, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:757-760, internal/statusreport/statusreport.go:108-110, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:3420-3426, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:3968-3972, internal/statusreport/parse.go:450-478, internal/runner/runner.go:737-749, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:484-491, internal/statusreport/parse_test.go:415-427, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main_test.go:3588-3598, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:485-491
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    parse.go
    455 	type usage struct{ cpu, mem string }
    456 	byPod := map[string]usage{}
    457 	for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
    458 		f := strings.Fields(line)
    459 		if len(f) < 4 {
    460 			continue
    461 		}
    462 		pod, container, cpu, mem := f[0], f[1], f[2], f[3]
    471 		u, ok := byPod[insts[i].Name]
    runner.go
    741 	case allNamespaces:
    742 		argv = append(argv, "--all-namespaces")
    749 	argv = append(argv, "--containers", "--no-headers")

Why it matters: kubectl's top printer prepends a NAMESPACE column whenever --all-namespaces is given (printSinglePodContainerMetrics writes namespace, pod, container, cpu, memory). KubernetesTop passes --all-namespaces under --all, so every row has five fields; the len(f) < 4 guard lets them through and the positional unpack shifts by one: pod is the namespace, container the pod, cpu the container name, mem the CPU. byPod is then keyed by namespace, which matches no instance name, so 'status container --all --details' on kubernetes prints no cpu/memory line for any pod and emits no note (kubectl succeeded): the enrichment the flag exists for vanishes silently. In the unlucky case of a pod named like its namespace, that pod's cpu would be a container name and Percent() silently yields ''. Independently the map is keyed by pod name alone while --all instances are namespaced -- the very collision status.go:757-760 guards against for the script run. No test covers --all with --details (the only top fixture, main_test.go:3424, is four columns without --all). Confirm with 'kubectl top pod --all-namespaces --containers --no-headers' on any cluster.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/statusreport/parse.go
+++ b/internal/statusreport/parse.go
@@ -452,23 +452,34 @@
-// "<pod> <container> <cpu> <memory>". Rows for a container this report is not
-// about are ignored, and a pod with no row keeps its limits and no usage.
+// "<pod> <container> <cpu> <memory>", or "<namespace> <pod> <container> <cpu>
+// <memory>" under --all-namespaces, where kubectl leads with the namespace.
+// Rows for a container this report is not about are ignored, and a pod with no
+// row keeps its limits and no usage.
 func ApplyTop(insts []Instance, out string) {
 	type usage struct{ cpu, mem string }
-	byPod := map[string]usage{}
+	type key struct{ ns, pod string }
+	byPod := map[key]usage{}
 	for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
 		f := strings.Fields(line)
 		if len(f) < 4 {
 			continue
 		}
+		ns := ""
+		if len(f) >= 5 {
+			ns, f = f[0], f[1:]
+		}
 		pod, container, cpu, mem := f[0], f[1], f[2], f[3]
+		k := key{ns, pod}
 		// Keep the connector container's row; for a single-container pod the name
 		// is whatever it is, so the first row for that pod wins.
-		if _, seen := byPod[pod]; seen && container != spec.ConnectorContainerName {
+		if _, seen := byPod[k]; seen && container != spec.ConnectorContainerName {
 			continue
 		}
-		byPod[pod] = usage{cpu, mem}
+		byPod[k] = usage{cpu, mem}
 	}
 	for i := range insts {
-		u, ok := byPod[insts[i].Name]
+		u, ok := byPod[key{insts[i].Namespace, insts[i].Name}]
+		if !ok {
+			u, ok = byPod[key{"", insts[i].Name}]
+		}
 		if !ok || insts[i].Container == nil {
 			continue
 		}
```

To confirm: Run `kubectl top pod --all-namespaces --containers --no-headers` against any cluster with metrics-server and count the fields per row (expect 5, namespace first); then run `status container --platform kubernetes --all --details` and check that no cpu/memory line appears. | Against any cluster with metrics-server: `kubectl top pod --all-namespaces --containers --no-headers | head -1 | wc -w` (expect 5: NAMESPACE POD NAME CPU MEMORY); then run `status container --platform kubernetes --all --details` and check that no cpu/memory lines are printed and no note explains it. | kubectl top pod --all-namespaces --containers --no-headers on any cluster with metrics-server: count fields per row (expect 5, namespace first).

Why it matters: Every charset gate here is a set of ASCII tests, so any rune >= 0x80 passes: SafeToken (image.repo/name/tag, timezone, docker/podman restart, roles), safeHostPath (tls.*.file, libs.dir, base-dir) and consolidate.needsQuote (every value render.q leaves plain). NEL, LINE SEPARATOR and PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR are line breaks in YAML 1.1 and in yaml.v3's scanner (quoted above; compose-go parses compose files with yaml.v3; kubectl's sigs.k8s.io/yaml and Spring's SnakeYAML share the libyaml/YAML 1.1 lineage). Steps: (1) env.yaml writes image.tag: "3.1.0<U+2028>x-evil: {}" or a destination with the same escape; (2) ParseEnv decodes the escape into the raw rune; (3) checkImage runs SafeToken -- no rune in the value is <= 0x20, 0x7f, a quote, or in shellMeta -- so no issue; (4) dockergen.go:113 writes ` image: solace/...:3.1.0<U+2028>x-evil: {}` as a plain scalar; (5) yaml.v3 ends the plain scalar at is_break, skip_line resets the column to 0 and the remaining text is parsed as a new top-level key, i.e. structure the spec never declared, while the project's own UnsafeTokenReason promises 'no spaces ... control chars'. The same shape applies to deploy.go:374/388 (manifest piped to kubectl) and, through needsQuote, to application.yml hosts/destinations. The author already controls env.yaml, so this is a bypass of the project's defence-in-depth rather than of a privilege boundary: major. Fix: make safeShellChars ASCII-only (no legitimate token, image ref, tz name or restart policy is non-ASCII), add the three break runes to safeHostPath (paths may legitimately be non-ASCII) and to needsQuote, update UnsafeTokenReason and the HTML port's copy of these functions.

#### CR-0350 [minor] [new] 'never written to disk' claim in README and userguide ignores compose writable layer and podman file driver

Location: README.md:38-45, docs/userguide.md:1413, docs/userguide.md:1512, docs/userguide.md:1756-1759, docs/userguide.md:2259-2260, internal/dockergen/dockergen.go:89-94, docs/userguide.md:1756-1768, docs/userguide.md:1614-1618, internal/dockergen/dockergen.go:89-104, internal/runner/runner.go:505-520, docs/userguide.md:1757-1767, README.md:38-42
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    userguide.md:1757-1759  - **docker**: compose `secrets:` using the **environment provider**, so values are read from the environment `docker compose` itself runs with -- the CLI injects them into that child process only. Nothing is written to disk. Requires **Docker Compose v2.23.1+**.
    userguide.md:1763-1767  - **podman**: `deploy` loads each credential into **podman's secret store** (values on stdin, never in argv) ...
    README.md:38-42  each credential ... is mounted as a file under `/app/external/var/secrets/` -- a Kubernetes Secret volume, a compose environment-provider secret, or a podman secret, never an environment variable and never written to disk as a value.
    dockergen.go:91-93  // ... so the value is read from the environment `docker compose` itself runs with -- it is never written to a file by this tool, and never appears in the compose document.
    runner.go:514  r.Run(Cmd{Argv: append(..., "secret", "create", name, "-"), Stdin: value})

Why it matters: The tool itself writes no value (the code comment at dockergen.go:91-93 is precise), but the docs generalise that to the engines. Docker Compose (non-swarm) materialises an environment-sourced secret by copying it into the container at the target path, which lands in the container's writable layer under the engine's storage root on the host; podman's default secret driver ('file') keeps secrets in a plain JSON file under the user's containers storage. The checklist asks that 'where the bytes rest [be] written down rather than assumed'. A reader of README.md:38-42 or userguide.md:1759 would conclude the credentials never touch the host disk on docker/podman, which is a decision they may need to make differently (e.g. an encrypted secret driver, or restricting the storage root). Suspected: engine internals were not inspected in this run; `docker inspect` of the container's upper dir and `podman secret inspect --showsecret` / the filedriver JSON would confirm. Fix is documentation: state per engine where the bytes rest and under whose ownership.

Change: as described above

To confirm: On a host with docker compose v2.23.1+: bring a service up with an environment-provider secret, then list <UpperDir>/app/external/var/secrets (UpperDir from docker inspect --format '{{.GraphDriver.Data.UpperDir}}'). For podman: podman secret create, then read the filedriver secretsdata.json under the containers storage dir (or podman secret inspect --showsecret).

#### CR-0351 [minor] [new] bash completion walker mis-walks --flag=value and URLs because COMP_WORDS splits on = and :

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:372-396, cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:376-381, cmd/solmq-conn-util/testdata/completions/solmq-conn-util.bash:109-118, cmd/solmq-conn-util/testdata/completions/solmq-conn-util.bash:124-147, cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:378, cmd/solmq-conn-util/testdata/completions/solmq-conn-util.bash:126-131, cmd/solmq-conn-util/testdata/completions/solmq-conn-util.bash:109-111
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    solmq-conn-util.bash:109-111  cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}" ... prev="${COMP_WORDS[$((COMP_CWORD - 1))]}"
    solmq-conn-util.bash:114-118  kind="$(_solmq_conn_util_flag_arg "$prev")" ... file) _solmq_conn_util_paths "$cur" file; return ;;
    solmq-conn-util.bash:126-131
        word="${COMP_WORDS[$i]}"
        case "$word" in
          -*=*) ;;   # --env=path carries its own value; nothing to skip
          -*)
            if [ -n "$(_solmq_conn_util_flag_arg "$word")" ]; then i=$((i + 1)); fi
    solmq-conn-util.bash:135-137  elif [ -z "$arg1" ]; then arg1="$word"; positional=$((positional + 1))
    completion.go:378  add("      -*=*) ;;   # --env=path carries its own value; nothing to skip")

Why it matters: bash's default COMP_WORDBREAKS is `"'><=;|&(:`, so readline hands the completion function `--env=env.yaml` as three COMP_WORDS: `--env`, `=`, `env.yaml`. Walking `generate --env=env.yaml <TAB>`: `--env` matches `-*)` (the `-*=*)` arm never sees a joined word), flag_arg says file, so `=` is skipped as the value; `env.yaml` then becomes arg1 and positional=1, and the script offers nothing instead of `config`. Completing the value itself, `generate --env=en<TAB>`, has prev=`=` and cur=`en`, so no file completion is offered either. The same split happens at `:` for `download jar mq --url https://repo/x.jar <TAB>`, where `https`, `:` and `//repo/x.jar` are counted as positionals. zsh's `words` and PowerShell's CommandElements do not split this way, so only bash is affected. Confirm by sourcing the script in bash with default COMP_WORDBREAKS and pressing TAB on those lines. The standard fix is to rejoin with `_get_comp_words_by_ref -n '=:' cur prev words cword` when bash-completion provides it (falling back to the current arrays), or to drop the `-*=*` claim from the script and the docs and state that the `=` form is not completed.

Change: as described above

To confirm: In bash with default COMP_WORDBREAKS, source the generated script and press TAB after 'solmq-conn-util generate --env=env.yaml ' (expect no 'config' candidate; COMP_WORDS is solmq-conn-util generate --env = env.yaml ''), after 'generate --env=en', and after 'download jar mq --url https://h/x.jar '.
