#### CR-0352 [minor] [new] >> $PROFILE recipe in the PowerShell header appends UTF-16LE under PS 5.1 and corrupts an existing profile

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:841-846, docs/userguide.md:157-160, cmd/solmq-conn-util/testdata/completions/solmq-conn-util.ps1:7-10, scripts/dev.ps1:43-44, cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:842-846, cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:843, docs/userguide.md:159, cmd/solmq-conn-util/testdata/completions/solmq-conn-util.ps1:8-10
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    userguide.md:158-159 `# PowerShell -- Register-ArgumentCompleter is per-session, so persist it` / `solmq-conn-util auto-complete powershell >> $PROFILE`
    completion.go:843-844 `"Register-ArgumentCompleter below is per-session, so appending to the",` / `"profile is what makes it stick:",` / `"solmq-conn-util auto-complete powershell >> $PROFILE",`
    testdata ps1:10 `#   solmq-conn-util auto-complete powershell >> $PROFILE`
    dev.ps1:43-44 `# Add-Content, never Tee-Object: Tee doubles lines and writes UTF-16.` / `Add-Content -Path (Get-Log $Task) -Value $line -Encoding utf8` (the project already knows and avoids this trap for its own logs)
    completion.go:849 `add("# Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatible: no &&/||, no ternary, no null-coalescing.")` (5.1 is an explicit target)

Why it matters: In Windows PowerShell 5.1 the `>`/`>>` operators are Out-File with its default 'Unicode' (UTF-16LE) encoding. The binary emits ASCII/LF; PowerShell decodes it and `>>` re-encodes it as UTF-16LE when appending. An existing ASCII/UTF-8 $PROFILE (the common case) then contains a UTF-8 head followed by UTF-16LE bytes with no BOM, which PowerShell reads as garbage on every start-up (`R e g i s t e r - ...` with NULs -> parse errors), breaking the profile the recipe was meant to extend. On a fresh machine `>>` also fails outright when `~\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\` does not exist. PowerShell 7 writes UTF-8 and is unaffected, but the script header declares 5.1 support. The fix is the same one dev.ps1 uses for its logs. Changing completion.go:844 regenerates the golden (`./scripts/dev.sh regen`).

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/docs/userguide.md
+++ b/docs/userguide.md
@@ -156,7 +156,11 @@
 
 ```powershell
 # PowerShell -- Register-ArgumentCompleter is per-session, so persist it
-solmq-conn-util auto-complete powershell >> $PROFILE
+# Add-Content -Encoding utf8, not >>: Windows PowerShell 5.1's >> appends
+# UTF-16LE, which corrupts an existing UTF-8/ASCII profile. The profile's
+# directory may not exist yet on a fresh machine.
+New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Split-Path $PROFILE) | Out-Null
+Add-Content -Path $PROFILE -Encoding utf8 -Value (solmq-conn-util auto-complete powershell)
 ```
```

To confirm: On Windows PowerShell 5.1 with an existing UTF-8 $PROFILE, run the documented '>> $PROFILE' recipe, Format-Hex the tail of the file (expect UTF-16LE bytes with no BOM after the UTF-8 text), then start a new session and look for profile parse errors; also run it with a missing profile directory.

#### CR-0353 [minor] [new] Exit 1 'signal: interrupt' from readLog on Ctrl-C when the follow child exits before cancel runs

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/logs.go:282-299, internal/runner/runner.go:231-260, internal/runner/runner.go:231-275
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    logs.go:287-293: `stop := make(chan os.Signal, 1); signal.Notify(stop, os.Interrupt); ... go func() { <-stop; cancel() }()`. logs.go:296-298: `if err := s.Stream(ctx, ...); err != nil { return errExit(fmt.Errorf("reading %s: %w", t.name, err)) }`. runner.go:267-274: `runErr := cmd.Run(); if ctx.Err() != nil { return nil }; return runErr`. logs.go:272-275 (comment): "Ctrl-C is how a follow is meant to end, so it exits 0 ... Stream reports a cancelled context as success, so there is nothing here to unpick." docs/userguide and commands.go logs Detail: "(Ctrl-C, which is a clean exit, not a failure)".

Why it matters: A terminal Ctrl-C delivers SIGINT to the whole foreground process group: the Go parent and `kubectl logs -f` at once. Two things then race: the parent's runtime hands the signal to `stop`, the goroutine wakes and calls cancel(); meanwhile the child handles its own SIGINT, exits, and the parent's cmd.Run() returns. Stream decides on `ctx.Err() != nil` after Run returns -- if the child's exit is reaped before cancel() has run, ctx.Err() is nil, Stream returns the ExitError ("signal: interrupt") and readLog prints an error and exits 1, contradicting the documented clean exit. The in-process path is normally faster than a child process exit, so the window is small, which is why this is suspected rather than verified; a test cannot pin it either, and none tries. Recording that an interrupt was seen and treating a post-interrupt error as the intended end narrows the window to the signal-delivery latency.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/logs.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/logs.go
@@ -10,4 +10,5 @@
 	"strings"
+	"sync/atomic"
 	"time"
@@ -282,4 +283,5 @@
 	ctx := context.Background()
+	var interrupted atomic.Bool
 	if o.follow {
@@ -290,4 +292,5 @@
 		go func() {
 			<-stop
+			interrupted.Store(true)
 			cancel()
 		}()
@@ -296,4 +299,9 @@
 	if err := s.Stream(ctx, runner.Cmd{Argv: argv}, os.Stdout, os.Stderr); err != nil {
+		if interrupted.Load() {
+			// The terminal delivered the same Ctrl-C to the child, which may have
+			// exited before cancel ran: the follow still ended on purpose.
+			return 0
+		}
 		return errExit(fmt.Errorf("reading %s: %w", t.name, err))
 	}
```

To confirm: On Linux, run logs --follow against a stub child that exits at once on SIGINT (or kubectl) from a terminal and press Ctrl-C many times; count runs that print 'signal: interrupt' and exit 1.


#### CR-0354 [minor] [new] On Windows a ':' in --allow-command/--command argv[0] is resolved as a path (no ErrDot), and PATHEXT can turn an allowlisted name into a .cmd/.bat run by cmd.exe

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:1215-1224, internal/validate/validate.go:1218-1222, internal/runner/runner.go:316-328, internal/runner/runner.go:1053, internal/runner/runner.go:1079
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    main.go:1216-1217 if strings.ContainsRune(s, '/') { return fmt.Errorf("--allow-command %q: a path is not accepted here; use a bare binary name, resolved from PATH", s) }
    validate.go:1219-1220 if binName := stripExe(bin); strings.Contains(binName, "/") { return fmt.Errorf("%q: a path is not accepted here; use a bare binary name, resolved from PATH", bin)
    validate.go:1446 const shellMeta = ";|&<>()*?[]{}~#!"   (':' is allowed; '\\' is rejected by safeShellChars)
    runner.go:320 resolved, err := exec.LookPath(c.Argv[0])
    /usr/local/go/src/os/exec/lp_windows.go lookPathExts: if strings.ContainsAny(file, `:\/`) { f, err := findExecutable(file, exts) ... }   -- treated as a path, PATH not searched, no ErrDot
    /usr/local/go/src/os/exec/lp_windows.go pathExt(): default exts .com .exe .bat .cmd; findExecutable appends each
    runner.go:1053 argv = append(argv, ContainerShell, "-c", "if [ -f "+path+" ]; then echo ...; fi")

Why it matters: 1. Both 'no path' gates test only for '/', while Go's Windows LookPath treats any token containing ':', '\\' or '/' as a path. SafeToken rejects the backslash but allows ':'. 2. `--allow-command C:evil --command C:evil` passes allowCommandValue.Set and CheckDeployCommand (extraAllowed match, no '/'), and exec.LookPath('C:evil') resolves it relative to the current directory of drive C without the ErrDot refusal the design relies on -- the escape hatch the operator typed defeats the 'bare PATH-resolved name' rule it was documented to keep. 3. Separately, a bare allowlisted name such as kubectl is completed through PATHEXT, so a kubectl.cmd or kubectl.bat wrapper earlier on PATH is what runs; CreateProcess executes those through cmd.exe, whose argument parsing re-interprets the ';', '[', ']' and '>' in the tool's own sh -c payloads (lines 1053, 1079) and '%' in any token -- the shell the design says is never involved. Both need a Windows run to confirm; the parser side is plain from the code. Rejecting ':' alongside '/' at both gates closes the first; the second is worth a sentence in the docs (accept only .exe) or a check that the resolved path ends in .exe on windows.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go
@@ -1215,5 +1215,7 @@ func (allowCommandValue) String() string { return "" }
 func (v allowCommandValue) Set(s string) error {
-	if strings.ContainsRune(s, '/') {
+	// ':' as well as '/': Go's Windows LookPath treats a token containing either
+	// as a path and resolves it without searching PATH or refusing ErrDot.
+	if strings.ContainsAny(s, "/:") {
 		return fmt.Errorf("--allow-command %q: a path is not accepted here; use a bare binary name, resolved from PATH", s)
 	}
--- a/internal/validate/validate.go
+++ b/internal/validate/validate.go
@@ -1218,3 +1218,3 @@ func CheckDeployCommand(platform, cmd string, extraAllowed []string) error {
 	bin := tokens[0]
-	if binName := stripExe(bin); strings.Contains(binName, "/") {
+	if binName := stripExe(bin); strings.ContainsAny(binName, "/:") {
 		return fmt.Errorf("%q: a path is not accepted here; use a bare binary name, resolved from PATH", bin)
```

To confirm: On Windows, run status or deploy with --allow-command C:x --command C:x with x.exe in drive C's current directory (expect it to run with no ErrDot refusal); and put a kubectl.bat that echoes %* ahead of kubectl.exe on PATH to see whether the sh -c payload survives cmd.exe.

 -- both are immutable once the object exists, so raising `storage` and redeploying
 looks like it worked but leaves the claim asking for more than the volume has.
-`deploy` warns, naming the volume, whenever it re-applies a PV that already existed;
+`deploy` warns, naming the volume, when kubectl reports an existing PV as `configured`;
 delete the volume and deploy again to change either setting.
```

If (2) updates the capacity or (3) errors, the guide's 'looks like it worked' premise and the warning text are wrong, not only the 'whenever' wording.

#### CR-0356 [minor] [new] The Deployment states no update strategy: a standalone (replicas 1) rollout runs the old and new connector side by side, unlike compose/quadlet which replace the container

Location: internal/deploy/deploy.go:323-331, internal/validate/validate.go:714-717, internal/deploy/deploy.go:462-471

    deploy.go:323-331  spec: / replicas: dep.Replicas / selector: / matchLabels: / app: name / template:   -- no strategy: key
    validate.go:714-717  mode := ctx.Defaults.LeaderElection.Mode / if (mode == "" || mode == spec.LeaderStandalone) && dep.Replicas > 1 { add(fileEnv, "leader-election standalone requires replicas: 1 (got %d)", dep.Replicas) }

    userguide.md:2327  Under quadlet a restart **recreates** the container   (podman: stop then start; compose up -d likewise replaces)

Why it matters: Kubernetes defaults to RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% (rounds up to 1) and maxUnavailable 25% (rounds down to 0), so a `rollout restart` or an image bump of a standalone instance starts the new pod while the old one is still consuming: two connectors share the same MQ durable subscription names and Solace queues until readiness flips. Standalone is defined by the tool as 'exactly one instance' (validate.go:714-717), and the other two platforms never overlap. Whether the overlap is harmless depends on the connector's binding semantics (an MQ durable subscription in use by the old pod makes the new pod's bind fail until the old one exits), which I could not check. Emitting `strategy: {type: Recreate}` for standalone, and leaving RollingUpdate for the leader-election modes that are built for overlap, would state the intent in the artifact; document either way.

Change: as described above

To confirm: On a cluster apply a standalone Deployment (replicas 1) with an MQ topic source and run kubectl rollout restart: check whether two connector pods are Running at once, whether the new pod's bind fails, and that kubectl get deploy -o jsonpath='{.spec.strategy}' shows RollingUpdate 25%/25%.

#### CR-0357 [minor] [new] Guaranteed QoS claim broken by the resource-less libs-download initContainer in renderDeployment

Location: internal/deploy/deploy.go:364-371, internal/deploy/deploy.go:508-513, docs/userguide.md:1341, internal/deploy/deploy.go:357-371, internal/deploy/deploy.go:508-523
Confidence: suspected

    internal/deploy/deploy.go:364-371
      w.Line(6, "initContainers:")
      w.Line(8, "- name: libs-download")
      w.Line(10, "image: "+d.Image)
      w.Line(10, `command: ["sh", "-c", `+strconv.Quote(strings.Join(cmds, " && "))+`]`)

Why it matters: Kubernetes assigns QoS Guaranteed only when every container in the pod, init containers included, has cpu and memory requests equal to limits. #### CR-0361 [minor] [new] No TimeoutStartSec in RenderQuadlet's [Service], so a first-start image pull races systemd's 90s default

      }

Why it matters: Quadlet's ExecStart is `podman run`, which pulls the image on first start; systemd's DefaultTimeoutStartSec is 90s, after which the start is killed and the unit marked failed. A 300-500 MB connector image over a slow registry link exceeds that, and -- given the Restart= value is dropped (finding on unless-stopped) -- the unit stays failed with 'start operation timed out' in the journal. #### CR-0362 [minor] [new] OS.Run and RunSplit have no deadline or cancellation: a hung engine blocks deploy, status and the watch loop indefinitely

Location: internal/runner/runner.go:166-178, internal/runner/runner.go:183-195, cmd/solmq-conn-util/status.go:919-939
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    runner.go:171-176
    171     cmd := exec.Command(resolved, c.Argv[1:]...)
    176     runErr := cmd.Run()
    runner.go:188-193 (RunSplit): the same, no context
    runner.go:236,251 (Stream is the only seam with a context and a WaitDelay)
    236     cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, resolved, c.Argv[1:]...)
    251     cmd.WaitDelay = streamWaitDelay
    status.go:926-938
    927         c.opts.now = time.Now()
    931         c.renderOnce(os.Stdout)
    932         select {
    933         case <-stop:
    936         case <-tick.C:

Why it matters: Every buffered exec -- the preflight probes, apply/delete, compose, the podman secret calls, systemctl, and all status queries -- runs with no timeout. `docker info` against a dead remote context, `podman info` while a machine is starting, or kubectl against a black-holed API server (its own --request-timeout defaults to 0) blocks the verb with no output and no error. Inside `status --watch`, signal.Notify has replaced the default SIGINT exit, so Ctrl-C is only acted on after renderOnce returns; on unix the child usually dies from the terminal's own SIGINT, which unblocks the loop, but a child that ignores it keeps the tool hung. Marked suspected because it needs a runtime to observe. Fix: exec.CommandContext with a per-call deadline (a probe needs a few seconds, a query well under a minute) and a WaitDelay, surfacing `timed out after Ns waiting for <argv[0]> ...` as the error; the Runner interface need not change if the deadline lives in OS.

Change: as described above

To confirm: Point docker or kubectl at an endpoint that accepts TCP but never replies, run deploy and 'status --watch', and observe that no deadline fires and how quickly Ctrl-C ends the watch while the child is blocked.

#### CR-0364 [minor] [new] resolveArgv0 accepts a .bat/.cmd resolution on Windows, reintroducing cmd.exe parsing that the SafeToken charset does not cover

Location: internal/runner/runner.go:316-328, internal/validate/validate.go:1194-1202, internal/validate/validate.go:1446-1454, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:199-206
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    runner.go:320 `resolved, err := exec.LookPath(c.Argv[0])` ... 327 `return resolved, nil`
    runner.go:171 `cmd := exec.Command(resolved, c.Argv[1:]...) //nolint:gosec // argv tokens are SafeToken-validated upstream; no shell is involved`
    validate.go:1195 `if s, ok := strings.CutSuffix(tok, ".exe"); ok {` / 1198 `if s, ok := strings.CutSuffix(tok, ".EXE"); ok {` (only .exe is anticipated)
    validate.go:1446 `const shellMeta = ";|&<>()*?[]{}~#!"` and safeShellChars (872-879) reject `<= 0x20, 0x7f, ' " \\ \` $` -- `%` and `^` pass.
    DEVELOPMENT.md:199-200 `shells out to the CLI named by each section's \`command:\` through an \`os/exec\` argv slice -- never \`sh -c\`.`

Why it matters: On Windows exec.LookPath("kubectl") tries every PATHEXT extension, so a `kubectl.cmd` or `oc.bat` wrapper (corporate shims, npm-style launchers) resolves and exec.Command runs it through cmd.exe, which re-parses the whole command line: `%VAR%` is expanded and `^` is an escape. Both characters pass SafeToken, so operator-supplied tokens such as `--namespace %TEMP%`, a `cli -- cat /x/%PATH%` argument or a `command: kubectl --context=%CTX%` value reach cmd.exe unquoted -- the exact shell layer the 'never sh -c' design excludes. Go's os/exec documents that it does not escape for cmd.exe. Suspected because it needs a batch wrapper on PATH; when present, the guard is bypassed by resolution rather than by any token. Refusing a batch-file resolution keeps the argv-only contract honest and the message tells the operator to point command: at the .exe.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/runner/runner.go
+++ b/internal/runner/runner.go
@@ -324,5 +324,11 @@
 		// exec.ErrDot); both cases are rejected here rather than silently exec'd.
 		return "", fmt.Errorf("resolving %q: %w", c.Argv[0], err)
 	}
+	// On Windows a name that resolves to a .bat/.cmd is run through cmd.exe,
+	// which re-parses the command line (%VAR% expansion, ^ escapes) -- a shell
+	// layer the SafeToken charset was never designed against. Refuse it.
+	if ext := strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(resolved)); ext == ".bat" || ext == ".cmd" {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("resolving %q: %s is a batch file, which Windows runs through cmd.exe; name the .exe instead", c.Argv[0], resolved)
+	}
 	return resolved, nil
 }
```

To confirm: On Windows put a kubectl.cmd shim that just echoes its arguments ahead of any kubectl.exe on PATH, set kubernetes.command to 'kubectl --context=%USERNAME%' and run deploy or status; if the shim prints the expanded user name, cmd.exe re-parsed the token.

#### CR-0365 [minor] [new] runner.Kubernetes deletes without --ignore-not-found, so a remove re-run exits 1 and skips removeNamespace

Location: internal/runner/runner.go:393-404, cmd/solmq-conn-util/main.go:546-556, internal/runner/runner.go:522-538
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    runner.go:398-403
    398     verb, err := kubeVerb(action)             // remove -> "delete"
    402     argv = append(argv, verb, "-f", "-")
    403     return r.Run(Cmd{Argv: argv, Stdin: manifest})
    main.go:548-555
    548     if code := report(action, tgtKubernetes, out, rerr); code != 0 {
    549         // A failed teardown leaves the namespace alone: whatever did not come
    550         // down is still in there.
    551         return code
    553     if action == runner.ActionRemove {
    554         return removeNamespace(r, o, e.Kubernetes)
    runner.go:522-523 (the podman side already handles this case): "PodmanSecretRemove deletes the named secrets, ignoring any that are already gone so a repeated delete stays quiet."

Why it matters: kubectl delete with a multi-document manifest deletes the objects that exist and reports NotFound for the rest, exiting 1. After any partial state -- a first remove interrupted mid-way, a deploy whose apply failed on a later document, or an operator who deleted one object by hand -- a remove run deletes what is left, exits 1 with `error: remove kubernetes failed`, and because of the early return never offers the empty namespace for removal. The verb is therefore not idempotent on kubernetes, while docker (`compose down` on nothing) and the podman secret removal (`--ignore`) were deliberately made so. Marked suspected because kubectl was not run here; `kubectl delete -f - <<< <manifest of absent objects>; echo $?` confirms the exit status. Fix: append --ignore-not-found on the remove verb (patch; TestKubernetesRemoveUsesDeleteVerb follows). The same NotFound issue applies to removeNamespace's own delete of an already-gone namespace.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/internal/runner/runner.go
+++ b/internal/runner/runner.go
@@ -399,6 +399,12 @@ func Kubernetes(r Runner, command, action, manifest string, extraAllowed []strin
 	if err != nil {
 		return "", err
 	}
 	argv = append(argv, verb, "-f", "-")
+	if action == ActionRemove {
+		// A document that is already gone is the outcome remove wants, not a
+		// failure: without this a re-run after a partial teardown exits 1 and
+		// never reaches the namespace step.
+		argv = append(argv, "--ignore-not-found")
+	}
 	return r.Run(Cmd{Argv: argv, Stdin: manifest})
 }
```

To confirm: kubectl delete -f - <<< '<manifest of an object that does not exist>'; echo $? -- expect 'Error from server (NotFound)' and exit 1; adding --ignore-not-found should give exit 0.

Location: internal/statusscript/statusscript_test.go:763-842, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:1-7, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:258-280, internal/statusscript/statusscript_test.go:763-817, internal/statusscript/statusscript.go:258-284
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    statusscript.go:4-7
    4: // produces targets the connector image's busybox userland (Alpine's sh, sed,
    5: // wget, tr, base64, head, cat, sort, cut -- no curl, no jq, no bash), so every
    6: // construct below is deliberately POSIX/busybox-safe rather than bash- or
    7: // GNU-coreutils-flavored.
    statusscript_test.go:765-773
    765: 	if sh, err := exec.LookPath("sh"); err == nil {
    766: 		return sh
    768: 	for _, sh := range []string{`C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe`, `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\sh.exe`} {
    773: 	t.Skip("no POSIX sh on PATH or in Git for Windows, so the rendered health parse cannot be run here")
    statusscript.go:283: 	-e 's/[^<]*<\([^>]*\)>[^<]*/\1\n/g' \   (a newline in a sed replacement, GNU and busybox accept it; POSIX does not promise it)

Why it matters: TestHealthParseIsKeyOrderIndependent runs health_status/health_components under whatever `sh` and `sed` the CI runner has: dash/bash with GNU sed on ubuntu-24.04, Git's bash with GNU sed on windows-2025. The script's own contract is busybox (statusscript.go:4-7), and the two sed implementations differ in exactly the corners this program leans on (`\n` in a replacement, labels and `t` across -e fragments, bracket expressions with `]` first). A construct GNU accepts and busybox rejects would pass CI and fail in every container, which is the class of regression dc3253b was. Separately, testShell's t.Skip (773) means the suite's single behavioural test is quietly excluded on a host with no sh; the checklist's 'CI runs the same tests ... no skip that quietly excludes the important ones' applies, though both current CI images do have one. Confirm by piping the same two function bodies and fixtures through `busybox sh` (an alpine container) and comparing with the GNU results; a cheap mitigation is to prefer a `busybox` binary when one is on PATH and to fail rather than skip when the SOLMQ_REQUIRE_SH environment variable is set in CI.

Change: as described above

To confirm: Run health_status and health_components plus the seven fixtures at statusscript_test.go:722-830 under busybox sh (an alpine container) and compare with the GNU sed results; not run here because this review is read-only.


#### CR-0372 [minor] [new] CheckDeployCommand lets a bare word follow a value-less flag, so `kubectl --warnings-as-errors krew` smuggles a subcommand/plugin past the flag-shaped rule

Location: internal/validate/validate.go:1225-1237, internal/validate/validate.go:1182-1184
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    validate.go:1225-1236
    1225 for i := 1; i < len(tokens); i++ {
    1226     tok := tokens[i]
    1227     switch {
    1228     case tok == "--":
    1229         return fmt.Errorf(`token "--": end-of-flags marker is not accepted`)
    1230     case strings.HasPrefix(tok, "-"):
    1231     case isAllowed(stripExe(tok)):
    1232     case strings.HasPrefix(tokens[i-1], "-") && !strings.Contains(tokens[i-1], "="):
    1233         // This token is the previous flag's value.
    1234     default:
    1235         return fmt.Errorf("token %q: arguments must be flag-shaped ...")
    validate.go:1182-1184 // Honest limitation: a flag's value is not further inspectable (arity is unknowable from the token stream alone), so the hard guarantee here covers argv[0] and every bare token -- not what a flag's value itself contains.

Why it matters: 1. The guard's stated guarantee is that every bare (non-flag) token is checked so 'solmq-conn-util appends its own subcommand'. 2. Because arity is unknown, any token after a dash-prefixed token without '=' is accepted as that flag's value -- including after a boolean flag that takes none. 3. `command: kubectl --warnings-as-errors krew` or `oc --insecure-skip-tls-verify evil` passes; kubectl sees `krew` as a positional, which its plugin mechanism resolves to a `kubectl-krew` binary on PATH, and `docker --debug buildx compose ...` reaches the docker-buildx CLI plugin the same way -- so a bare word is executed as a subcommand after all, with the tool's appended argv (apply -f -, exec ..., info) as its arguments. 4. The env.yaml author can only reach plugins the operator already has, and the appended argv limits what they can do, so this is defense in depth rather than a live hole -- but the 'bare token' guarantee the comment makes does not hold, and the limitation note should say so (or the rule should accept a bare value only after flags from a small known-arity list).

Change: as described above

To confirm: Run the installed docker and kubectl with '--flag <word>', and 'sudo -n sh -c <word>' under --allow-command sudo, to confirm the downstream CLI treats the bare word as a subcommand or command. Needs a runtime; not run here.

Tags: security


#### CR-0373 [nit] [new] graphify hook-guard hooks in .claude/settings.json have no guard for a missing graphify binary

Location: .claude/settings.json:5-10, .claude/settings.json:15-20, scripts/dev.sh:148-148, scripts/dev.ps1:162-164
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    .claude/settings.json:5-10:   "matcher": "Bash|Grep", ... "type": "command", "command": "graphify hook-guard search", "timeout": 10
    .claude/settings.json:15-20:  "matcher": "Read|Glob", ... "command": "graphify hook-guard read", "timeout": 10
    scripts/dev.sh:148:   command -v graphify >/dev/null || { warn "graphify not on PATH; skipping"; return 0; }
    scripts/dev.ps1:162-164: if (-not (Get-Command graphify -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Warn 'graphify not on PATH; skipping'; return 0 }
    git log: 2d3cdf5 "updated claude files to be host os agnostic"

Why it matters: The project-level settings file is shared with everyone who clones the repo and opens it in Claude Code; it runs `graphify hook-guard ...` before every Bash, Grep, Read and Glob call. The dev scripts treat graphify as optional and warn-skip when it is missing (dev.sh:148, dev.ps1:162-164), but the hook has no such guard, so on a machine without graphify each of those tool calls would first fail a hook (command not found) and surface that error on every step -- noisy at best, blocking at worst depending on how the harness treats a non-zero hook exit. Build checklist: 'no reliance on tools that happen to be on the developer's machine'. Suspected because the hook's failure semantics are outside the repo, and because the command was kept deliberately shell-agnostic (2d3cdf5), a POSIX `command -v` guard would not fit; options are documenting the graphify prerequisite in DEVELOPMENT.md or moving the hooks to the untracked settings.local.json. No patch offered for that reason.

Change: as described above

To confirm: Open the repo in Claude Code on a host without graphify on PATH, run any Bash/Read/Grep/Glob call, and check whether the PreToolUse hook error (exit 127) blocks the call or only prints a notice.


#### CR-0374 [nit] [new] abbrevTable sorts with sort.Slice on Short only; a repeated alias spelling would make the doc nondeterministic

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/abbreviation.go:26-32, cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion_test.go:452-492, cmd/solmq-conn-util/abbreviation_doc_test.go:55-63, cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion_test.go:462-475
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    abbreviation.go:29-32  // Aliases are unique across the model, so the ordering is total and the output\n// byte-stable.\nfunc abbrevTable(...) {\n	sort.Slice(rows, func(i, j int) bool { return rows[i].Short < rows[j].Short })
    completion_test.go:468-474  for _, a := range tg.Aliases { ... for _, other := range v.Targets { if other.Name == a { t.Errorf("%q target alias %q collides with target %q", ...) } } }   -- only within one verb, only against canonical names
    abbreviation_doc_test.go:55-58  // Set comparison rather than a row count, so two kinds of abbreviation that ever share a spelling (a verb alias and a target alias under another verb) do not read as a spurious extra row.

Why it matters: The comment asserts uniqueness, but the gate that enforces alias uniqueness covers verb aliases only; two targets under different verbs may share an alias (the sibling test even anticipates it), and then two rows in the target table have equal Short keys. sort.Slice is not stable, so their order can differ between runs and TestAbbreviationDocInSync would flap. A stable sort with a tiebreak on the remaining cells keeps the output byte-stable under every model the tests allow.

Suggested patch (not applied):

```diff
--- a/cmd/solmq-conn-util/abbreviation.go
+++ b/cmd/solmq-conn-util/abbreviation.go
@@ -32 +32,6 @@
-	sort.Slice(rows, func(i, j int) bool { return rows[i].Short < rows[j].Short })
+	sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
+		if rows[i].Short != rows[j].Short {
+			return rows[i].Short < rows[j].Short
+		}
+		return strings.Join(rows[i].Cells, "|") < strings.Join(rows[j].Cells, "|")
+	})
```

To confirm: a runtime check against a real engine; see the description


#### CR-0375 [nit] [new] fish target conditions match flag values, so `status --namespace all <TAB>` or `--pod app` hides the target menu

Location: cmd/solmq-conn-util/completion.go:729-740, cmd/solmq-conn-util/testdata/completions/solmq-conn-util.fish:38-46, cmd/solmq-conn-util/testdata/completions/solmq-conn-util.bash:126-131
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    solmq-conn-util.fish:39  complete -c solmq-conn-util -n '__fish_seen_subcommand_from status sts; and not __fish_seen_subcommand_from container cnt application app all' -a 'container' ...
    solmq-conn-util.fish:38  ... -n '__fish_seen_subcommand_from generate gen; and not __fish_seen_subcommand_from config cfg' -a 'config' ...
    completion.go:734-735  cond := "__fish_seen_subcommand_from " + fishSeenNames(v) + "; and not __fish_seen_subcommand_from " + itemSeenNames(v.Targets)
    solmq-conn-util.bash:129-131  -*) if [ -n "$(_solmq_conn_util_flag_arg "$word")" ]; then i=$((i + 1)); fi   -- bash (and zsh/powershell) skip a flag's value before counting positionals

Why it matters: `__fish_seen_subcommand_from` tests every token after the command name, flag values included. A namespace called `all`, a pod whose name is `app` or a container called `cnt`, typed as `status --namespace all <TAB>`, satisfies the `not ... all` clause and fish stops offering container/application/all, while bash, zsh and PowerShell skip flag values first and still offer them. Short aliases (`app`, `cnt`, `cfg`) make the collision likelier than it looks. Confirm in fish by typing the lines above. The usual remedy is a small helper function emitted into the script that counts positionals after skipping flag values (fish has `commandline -opc`), used in place of the bare seen-check for Targets and Sets.

Change: as described above

To confirm: In fish, source the generated script, type 'solmq-conn-util status --namespace all ' and press TAB; confirm no container/application/all menu appears (and that it does appear without the flag).

#### CR-0377 [nit] [new] TCP logback variant sends bare pattern lines through LogstashTcpSocketAppender, with no syslog PRI or framing, although configured as 'syslog'

Location: internal/logback/logback.go:73-97, docs/userguide.md:959, internal/logback/logback.go:76-97
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    logback.go:73-74: 'sends newline-framed lines over TCP via logstash-logback-encoder's LogstashTcpSocketAppender'
    logback.go:89: <pattern>${SYSLOG_APPNAME}[%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>
    logback.go:49-50 (UDP): SyslogAppender with facility LOCAL0 and a suffixPattern

Why it matters: The UDP variant uses SyslogAppender, which adds the RFC 3164 PRI header and facility. The TCP variant, still configured as logging.syslog with protocol tcp, sends plain text lines with no PRI. A strict syslog receiver will mis-parse severity and facility or treat the lines as malformed. The same logging.syslog configuration therefore behaves differently per protocol, and the difference is documented only in a code comment. Check whether the user guide states this before treating it as a defect.

Change: as described above

To confirm: Optional: send a tcp line to a strict RFC 5424 or 3164 receiver and observe the parsed severity and facility.

Tags: parity, probe

```

#### CR-0379 [nit] [new] copyText has no rejection handler and dlText/downloadAll revoke the object URL synchronously after click

Location: solmq-conn-util-generator.html:3085, solmq-conn-util-generator.html:3086-3093, solmq-conn-util-generator.html:3101-3105
Confidence: suspected
Evidence:

    3085 function copyText(text){ navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(() => toast('Copied to clipboard')); }
    3089   a.href = URL.createObjectURL(b);
    3091   a.click();
    3092   URL.revokeObjectURL(a.href);

Why it matters: navigator.clipboard is undefined outside a secure context (a page served over plain http from an intranet host) so copyText throws synchronously, and a permission denial rejects the promise; both leave the user with no toast and no message. revokeObjectURL right after click() is a documented race in some browsers (the download may not have started reading the blob); deferring the revoke to a setTimeout or a load event is the usual shape. Confirming either needs a browser, hence suspected.

Change: as described above

To confirm: Open the page over plain http on a non-localhost host and click Copy (expect a TypeError and no toast); trigger a download in Safari or an older Firefox to see whether the synchronous revoke aborts the blob read.

- Completeness critic critic:1: gaps_remain -- The 46 lanes cover the main flows well, but coverage is thin on the three renderers (deploy, dockergen, podmangen), render.go 80-225, consolidate.go 1-300, and several unread ranges in validate.go. The generator page's JS port is unchecked against Go, and statusscript and the CI and dev scripts have inconsistent or partial read claims. Several lanes with few close reads (S7, T1, LEAD1, S6, T2, PARA) filed many test-gap or external-behaviour findings that deserve a spot-check. Eight probes are proposed, with the renderers, the render and consolidate core, and validate.go as the highest-yield ones.
- Completeness critic critic:2: gaps_remain -- Round 1 left the three CI/release files entirely unread, though several findings cite tag.yml. The main renderers (deploy, dockergen, podmangen), the middle sections of validate.go, consolidate.go and render.go, and parts of status.go and runner.go had only skim or grep coverage. I name 7 probes; the highest yield is a full read of the three renderers, and the CI workflow read and a validate.go section read follow.

- Stacks with core checklist only: PowerShell (scripts/dev.ps1), HTML/JavaScript (solmq-conn-util-generator.html)
- Dynamic checks not run: docker compose config on a rendered compose file (the run pasted had no file and validated nothing); /usr/libexec/podman/quadlet -dryrun -user on a rendered unit; shellcheck, actionlint, hadolint, staticcheck and golangci-lint are not installed on the review host and were not installed. Run by the user and folded into Dynamic checks: ./scripts/dev.sh vet, go test -race ./..., go mod tidy -diff, bash -n scripts/dev.sh
- Limits: read-only review: no build, test, scan, graph refresh or external tool was executed, so every statement about systemd, kubectl, docker, podman, busybox wget/sed, compose-go or browser behaviour is inferred from documentation and source, not observed; the knowledge graph was reused two commits stale and never queried (a query rewrites a tracked file); the connector image runtime user and capability needs are not in the tree, so the posture findings state what is emitted, not what the image tolerates; the BUILD_TARGETS and SHIP_IMAGE repository variables and branch protection are not in the checkout; .github/workflows/ci.yml, tag.yml and dependabot.yml were opened only by the C1/PARF lanes and the phase-4 CI probe, so their line coverage is thin; the completeness critic flagged lanes S7, T1, T2, LEAD1, PARA, S6 and SEC1 for filing many findings against few close reads, and their minor/nit test-gap claims carry that caveat; PowerShell and the HTML/JavaScript generator were reviewed on the core checklist only; the 25-finding cap per lane left overflow titles unverified
